## Finding

### Context the reader needs

This finding operates inside an ongoing chain of refinements to a single cognitive discipline called **articulate_simple** — a five-operation discipline (Itemize / Meta-question / Deconstruct / MultiDepth / Rephrase) that takes a compact task statement and expands it into a per-item bundle the rest of the project's cognitive loop can work with. The discipline-explainer document for articulate_simple lives at `devdocs/how_articulate_simple_should_be.md` and is referenced throughout this finding by section number (§1, §2.4, §2.5, etc.). The discipline is committed to **substrate-bounded operation** per §1 of the doc — it does not fetch project files, read recent inquiry history, or load specific artifacts. The substrate is the task statement plus the LLM's general knowledge plus any session context already loaded.

The 21-52 finding (which this finding refines specifically on the MultiDepth dimension) established a **substrate-bounded chain**: substrate-bounded ⇒ any commitment the LLM makes about properties of the task is a guess (no project context to ground it on) ⇒ downstream consumers (other operations in articulate-simple's flow + the runner formulating input for the next discipline /surfacing + the user reading the framing to verify it) treat the guess as actionable ⇒ downstream operations propagate the guess as if it were grounded. The 21-52 verdict applied that chain to Meta-question commitments and narrowed Meta-question's permissive-answer range from four shapes (identified-ambiguity / confident commitment / hedged commitment / explicit-empty) to two shapes (identified-ambiguity / explicit-empty).

The 21-52 finding flagged **MultiDepth's purpose-wrapped output** as Cascade 1 — the same critique should apply, but the specific resolution was deferred to a follow-up inquiry per the cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern (which says: name structural cascades honestly; defer their specific resolutions to follow-up inquiries with their own scope). This finding is that follow-up inquiry.

The user's request, verbatim: *"based on devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-06_21-52__no_commitments_pre_surfacing_safety/finding.md u said [the Cascade 1 prose quote about MultiDepth's purpose-wrapped suffering the same critique] lets dive deeper into this one."*

### What MultiDepth currently emits (background)

Under the current §2.4 of the discipline-explainer document, MultiDepth emits exactly two outputs per item:

- **Literal** — the task at its narrowest accurate framing. What is being asked, expressed precisely, with no purpose wrapping.
- **Purpose-wrapped** — the literal task INCLUDED in its perceived purpose chain. The text contains the literal task verbatim or near-verbatim, then chains its perceived purposes via causal connectives ("in order to" / "so we can" / equivalents).

Example from §2.4 (warm-context case for the input "improve auth module" with session context indicating a recent token-validation bug discussion):
- Literal: *"fix the token validation bug discussed"*
- Purpose-wrapped: *"fix login bug due to token validation in order to enable login feature for users, so we can login and test other features"*

The §2.4 INCLUDES-with-accuracy rule (load-bearing) requires purpose-wrapped to preserve the literal task verbatim; the rule prevents drift to a different task. §2.4 also commits MultiDepth to substrate-compliance — the purpose chain is inferred from the task statement + general knowledge (cold context) or session context (warm context); MultiDepth does not fetch from the project. The substrate boundary, in the doc's own words, "is the same as elsewhere in articulate."

This last commitment — that MultiDepth's substrate is the same as the rest of articulate-simple — is the structural ground that makes the substrate-bounded chain transfer cleanly. We'll return to it.

### The user is structurally right

The substrate-bounded chain from the 21-52 finding extends to MultiDepth's purpose-wrapped output symmetrically. The reasoning is structurally tight:

The substrate is identical. §2.4's substrate-compliance paragraph says explicitly: "MultiDepth does not fetch from the project. The substrate boundary is the same as elsewhere in articulate." When the LLM emits a purpose-wrapped output at the articulate-simple stage, it has no project context. The perceived purpose chain is necessarily a guess derived from the task statement + general knowledge + any session context.

Downstream consumers act on the guess. Rephrase (specified in §2.5 of the doc as varying "within the perceived scope, context-need, intent, and coherence" from Meta-question answers) reads MultiDepth's output as input — §1.1 of the doc commits "Deconstruct and MultiDepth's outputs are additional structure to vary along." The user reads the framing to verify it. Whichever consumers act on the purpose-wrapped output treat the LLM's perceived purpose chain as actionable framing.

This is contamination. A pre-context guess propagates through downstream framing as if it were grounded. Whatever the LLM perceived in cold context — "to improve readability" for a rename, "to enable login feature" for a token-validation fix — becomes the framing downstream operates within.

### Why the structural-property differences don't exempt MultiDepth

MultiDepth has five structural properties that differ from Meta-question commitments. Each is real; none reaches the contamination layer. We tested them one by one (this is the work Sensemaking did at Phase 2 perspective-checking + Phase 3 ambiguity-collapse).

**The INCLUDES-with-accuracy rule** anchors purpose-wrapped to literal verbatim. The rule prevents drift to a different task — purpose-wrapped can't morph "fix the token validation bug" into "redesign the OAuth flow." But the rule operates at the intra-MultiDepth integrity layer (drift between tasks); it does not prevent the perceived purpose chain from being wrong on the same task. Wrong-purpose-on-correct-task contamination is still possible.

**The literal output as fallback.** Downstream consumers have access to the literal output as a kind of ground truth — if they distrust purpose-wrapped, they can fall back to literal. This is a real structural mitigation that Meta-question commitments lack. But the default reading is still purpose-wrapped; consumers don't have a protocol that tells them to discount purpose-wrapped under cold context. The bias remains in the default reading.

**The perceivability principle.** §2.4 commits MultiDepth to not pad — it emits depth proportional to perceivable depth. This is substrate-honest behavior about DEPTH (how many connectives the chain has). It says nothing about CORRECTNESS (what the perceived purpose IS). A shallow chain in cold context can be substrate-honest about depth and still be a wrong guess about purpose.

**The rendering-vs-committing axis.** §2.4 says MultiDepth "renders depth of meaning." One could argue "rendering" is different in kind from "committing" — that rendering is making visible what's there rather than adjudicating what the answer is. The argument fails in cold context: rendering a perceived purpose chain IS committing to a perceived purpose chain when there's no project context to perceive against. The verb-distinction holds when there's substrate to perceive; it collapses when there isn't.

**The PATH-vs-ENDPOINT axis from MQ3.** The 22-44 finding distinguished MultiDepth from MQ3 (Meta-question 3, which infers user intent) on the basis that MultiDepth emits a PATH (literal + chain) while MQ3 emits an ENDPOINT (single statement of perceived intent). This distinction keeps the two operations from collapsing into each other. But it doesn't address substrate-bounded contamination; both PATH-form and ENDPOINT-form can carry guesses.

None of these five properties reaches the layer where the substrate-bounded chain operates. The chain runs: substrate-bounded ⇒ guess ⇒ downstream-bias-as-actionable ⇒ contamination. The properties operate at different layers: INCLUDES at intra-bundle integrity; literal-fallback at consumer-recovery; perceivability at depth-bound; rendering-vs-committing at verb-meaning; PATH-vs-ENDPOINT at form-shape. The 21-52 finding's K2 scope-mismatch crux explains exactly this: PERMISSION-style mitigations operate at the LLM-emission scope (authorizing hedged output), while contamination operates at the consumer scope (the consumer acts on whatever they receive). The layers don't connect. The same structural pattern applies here: MultiDepth's structural-property defenses operate at scopes that don't reach the contamination concern.

### The runner-bias claim from 21-52 is non-fatal but should be honest

The 21-52 finding's Cascade 1 prose said: *"Downstream consumers (the runner reading the purpose-wrapped to bias /surfacing toward the perceived purpose; the user reading the framing to verify it) act on the guessed purpose."* This named two downstream consumers: the runner (formulating input for the /surfacing discipline) and the user (verifying the framing).

But the runner-bias claim is not grounded in current §12 of the discipline-explainer document. §12's one-paragraph summary of articulate-simple says, in part: "The runner reads the Meta-question's MQ2 + MQ4 entries (preparation substrate + exclusions) and uses them to formulate the project's /surfacing discipline's input." Purpose-wrapped is not listed as a runner read.

This means the 21-52 Cascade 1 prose runner-bias claim may be speculative pending §12 clarification. Two interpretations are possible: either §12 is incomplete and the runner does in fact use purpose-wrapped (in which case the runner-bias claim is correct and §12 needs amendment), or §12 is correct and the runner-bias claim was a speculative addition in the 21-52 prose (in which case the runner-bias claim should be flagged speculative and the contamination case should rest on the confirmed downstream consumers).

The contamination case is robust either way. Rephrase is a confirmed consumer (per §1.1 of the doc). The user is a confirmed consumer (the user reads the per-item bundle). Two confirmed consumers are sufficient grounding for the contamination case.

### The verdict — REFINE-only-purpose-wrapped

Under the verdict, MultiDepth at articulate-simple stage emits per item:

- **Literal** — the task at its narrowest accurate framing. **Unchanged from current §2.4.** Literal preserves the input verbatim or near-verbatim; it carries no commitment to a perceived property of the task; per the new LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT structural insight (below), literal is structurally non-contaminating.

- **Purpose-ambiguity** — narrowed to a 2-shape range:
  1. **Identified-purpose-ambiguities** — when the LLM perceives openness about why the task is being requested. The output names the plausible purposes the task statement (plus general knowledge, plus session context) is consistent with, without committing to one. Example: for "Refactor the authentication module" under cold context, *"Purpose-motivation ambiguity: refactor could be for security hardening, for adding new auth methods, for cleaning up technical debt, or for migration to a different auth provider. Without project context, multiple purposes are plausible."*
  2. **Explicit-empty** — when no purpose-ambiguity is perceivable along the WHY axis. Example: for "rename foo to bar" with no session goals visible, the output is *"No specific purpose-ambiguity perceivable from the task statement at cold context"* (consistent with the 18-21 finding's empty-as-content principle: when ambiguity is not perceivable, emit explicit-empty rather than fabricate).

The slot for MultiDepth's second output is preserved (the 00-47 finding's Fixed-2 schema stays at 2 outputs per item). The content shape of that slot changes from commitment to identification.

The §2.4 INCLUDES-with-accuracy rule preserves its scope at the literal output. The rule no longer applies to the second output — identified-purpose-ambiguities lists plausible purposes rather than including the literal task verbatim in a wrapped chain. The rule's load-bearing role (preventing drift to a different task) is preserved for the literal half of the bundle.

The §2.4 substrate-compliance paragraph is preserved unchanged. The substrate boundary stays the same: no project-fetch; session-context allowed.

### Why this verdict is surgical — the LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT insight

A blanket refinement might have narrowed both literal and purpose-wrapped. We didn't, because of a structural insight that emerged in the analysis:

Within a multi-output bundle from an upstream substrate-bounded discipline, an output that preserves the input verbatim (or at its narrowest accurate framing) carries no commitment beyond the preservation itself — the LLM hasn't added any perceived content; it has just expressed the input in a clean form. There's nothing to contaminate. The contamination concern only applies to outputs that ADD perceived content based on the LLM's guess.

For MultiDepth, the literal output is input-preservation; the purpose-wrapped output was additive-content. Only the additive output needs to narrow. Literal stays unchanged.

This is the **LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT** insight. It applies broadly to multi-output bundles from upstream substrate-bounded disciplines — anywhere an upstream discipline emits both an input-preservation output and an additive-content output, the same surgical refinement pattern can be considered. The pattern's precondition is load-bearing: it applies **when the literal output is genuine input-preservation, not a curated paraphrase that secretly commits to a perceived framing.** When the precondition holds, the pattern enables surgical refinement; when it doesn't, the literal output may itself be contaminating and the analysis must extend to it.

Confirming evidence from neighboring domains was already in hand from the 21-52 finding's cross-domain validation work: compilers distinguish PARSE (syntactic identification of structure, no semantic commitment) from SEMANTIC ANALYSIS (commitment to meaning, after grammar binding completes). Parsers preserve input structure as an AST without committing meaning; semantic analyzers commit meaning post-binding. The structural distinction matches.

### Why MultiDepth's identity is preserved under refinement — the AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction

Under refinement, both MultiDepth (via identified-purpose-ambiguities) and MQ3 (via identified-intent-ambiguities per the 21-52 narrowing) become ambiguity-identification operations. A real concern arises: do they collapse into the same operation?

The 22-44 finding distinguished MultiDepth from MQ3 via the PATH-vs-ENDPOINT axis — MultiDepth emits a PATH (literal + chain); MQ3 emits an ENDPOINT (single statement of perceived intent). Under refinement, MultiDepth no longer emits a PATH; it emits a list of plausible purposes. MQ3 no longer emits an ENDPOINT; it emits a list of plausible intents. The PATH-vs-ENDPOINT distinction loses its surface form.

But the distinction shifts to a different structural axis — the **AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction**. MultiDepth identifies purpose-motivation ambiguities — the WHY axis (why the user wants the task done; motivation chain). MQ3 identifies intent-action ambiguities — the WHAT axis (what the user is trying to accomplish; action endpoint). These are genuinely different ambiguity dimensions even when the surface words overlap:

For "Refactor the authentication module" in cold context:
- MQ3-refined identifies intent-action ambiguities: "Is this iterate-on-existing or greenfield-rebuild?" (different actions)
- MultiDepth-refined identifies purpose-motivation ambiguities: "Is this for security hardening / for adding new auth methods / for cleaning up tech debt?" (different motivations)

In software-engineering vocabulary, "purpose" commonly maps to motivation/why (cf. "what's the purpose of this code") and "intent" to user-goal/what (cf. "what does the user intend to accomplish"). The distinction is clean in technical engineering vocabulary, though sometimes fuzzy in colloquial use — which is why this finding flags it for monitoring (Open Questions section below).

The operation-name "MultiDepth" is preserved on structural grounds. Under refinement, MultiDepth still renders something at a depth axis — it renders the openness of the purpose-motivation axis as identified ambiguity-richness in internal text (the carrier mechanism the 00-47 finding committed, now applied to ambiguity-richness rather than connective count). The user has the final call on the name per the 19-06 finding's asymmetric-naming-implies-output-identity meta-pattern (which was preserved at the 20-29 finding with the user-has-final-call note).

### What gets preserved unchanged or with scope refinement

Six structural features from prior commitments survive REFINE intact or with scope refinement:

1. **The 00-47 Fixed-2 schema** stays — MultiDepth still emits exactly two outputs per item (literal + purpose-ambiguity).
2. **The 00-47 depth-carrier mechanism** (depth lives in the text of the second output, not in output count) is preserved structurally. The carrier refines to ambiguity-richness in the internal text (how many plausible purposes the identified-purpose-ambiguities list names, with what cross-relationships) rather than connective count in a purpose-wrapped chain.
3. **The §2.4 INCLUDES-with-accuracy rule** is preserved for the literal output. Its scope tightens — it no longer applies to the second output (which lists plausible purposes rather than wrapping the literal).
4. **The §2.4 substrate-compliance paragraph** is preserved unchanged.
5. **The 11-16 PERMISSION-not-CONSTRAINT framing** is inherited as the 21-52 finding refined it. PERMISSION applies to articulate2 post-/surfacing commitments where hedging is appropriate; it does not apply to MultiDepth at the articulate-simple stage under this verdict. (Should the project later resolve Cascade C and adopt an articulate2 stage, PERMISSION would extend to MultiDepth-at-articulate2 too.)
6. **The 19-06 asymmetric-naming meta-pattern** is preserved with the user-has-final-call note. The operation-name "MultiDepth" stays on structural grounds; the user can elect a different name if they prefer.

### Three cascades named honestly without pre-decision

The verdict's substantive scope is bounded to the MultiDepth purpose-wrapped narrowing. But three cascading implications follow structurally. Per the 21-52 cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern, this finding names them honestly and explicitly does not pre-decide them.

**Cascade A — immediate doc revisions.** §2.4 essence sentence + §2.4 worked examples + §12 one-paragraph + §11 inheritance map. This finding's own substantive deliverable. User-authorized when ready (the specific COULDs are listed in Next Actions below).

**Cascade B — Rephrase's constraint source compounded.** §2.5 of the discipline-explainer document commits Rephrase to vary "within the perceived scope, context-need, intent, and coherence" from Meta-question answers, plus within the framing from MultiDepth's outputs (per §1.1 commitment). The 21-52 finding removed Meta-question commitments as Rephrase's constraint source (because Meta-question commitments became identified-ambiguities, not committed frames). This finding removes the remaining purpose-wrapped frame as a Rephrase constraint source (because purpose-wrapped becomes identified-purpose-ambiguities, not a committed frame). After this verdict, Rephrase has zero constraint sources at articulate-simple stage; Rephrase reduces to vocabulary-variation without semantic constraint. Whether that reduces Rephrase below viability, or whether Rephrase reconceives around varying-across-ambiguity-space, or whether Rephrase defers to articulate2 — these are open. Follow-up inquiry needed.

**Cascade C — §9 two-pass deferral pressure compounded.** §9 of the discipline-explainer document commits articulate-simple as "complete on its own — it produces a useful, defended framing in one pass," with the two-pass design (articulate-simple → /surfacing → articulate2) explicitly out of scope. The 21-52 finding put pressure on this commitment; this finding deepens the pressure. Under this verdict, articulate-simple cannot safely commit perceptions alone; it is complete as pre-context framing (useful for /surfacing's input formulation, useful for the user's framing verification) but not as final framing for downstream commitments. The two-pass design may become structurally necessary rather than optional. Follow-up inquiry needed.

### Two meta-patterns from 21-52 carry forward; one new pattern surfaced

The 21-52 finding's **substrate-contamination-vs-downstream-bias** meta-pattern (the layer-mismatch crux: PERMISSION-style mitigations at the emitter; downstream-bias at the consumer; the layers don't connect) is transferred to MultiDepth in this finding. The pattern's transferability is evidenced at sample-size 1 (this case); broader cross-discipline test deferred. The intentionally hedged language ("evidenced at sample-size 1" not "confirmed universally") avoids overclaim until cross-discipline tests provide more positive instances.

The 21-52 finding's **cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision** meta-pattern is reused consistently in this finding — the three cascades above are named honestly with their specific resolutions deferred.

The new **LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT** structural insight is the third pattern surfaced here. It applies within multi-output bundles from upstream substrate-bounded disciplines. Its precondition is that the literal output must be genuine input-preservation, not a curated paraphrase that secretly commits to a perceived framing. When the precondition holds, the pattern enables surgical refinement; when it doesn't, the literal output may itself need refinement.

The three patterns assemble into an **emergent reusable pattern: surgical-refinement-within-multi-output-bundles.** Components — substrate-bounded chain transferred to a new upstream-discipline output + AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction (where applicable) + LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT enabling surgical scope + cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision discipline for downstream implications. The assembly is reusable for future cascade resolutions in this chain.

- **Evidence**: Fixed-2 schema is preserved structurally (still 2 outputs: literal + purpose-ambiguity, where previously it was literal + purpose-wrapped). Internal-text-rendering as depth-carrier is preserved but the carrier shifts from connective count in a purpose-wrapped chain to ambiguity-richness in the identified-purpose-ambiguities list text. The Refinement-trigger to Bounded-variable preserves its observable-based trigger; its scope shifts to observing ambiguity-richness telemetry rather than output-count telemetry.

**Commitment 7**: the 22-44 finding's MultiDepth corrected essence (depth-of-meaning rendering + INCLUDES-with-accuracy rule + MQ3 endpoint-vs-path distinction).
- **Source**: `devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-05_22-44__multiscope_depth_of_meaning_correction/finding.md`.
- **Re-test status**: **RE-TESTED — REFINED**.
- **Evidence**: depth-of-meaning rendering essence shifts to "renders literal task + perceives purpose openness" — meaning-layer revision. INCLUDES-with-accuracy is preserved for the literal output; its scope tightens (no longer applies to the second output). MQ3 endpoint-vs-path distinction refines to AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction (purpose-motivation vs intent-action) under refinement; the structural distinction holds at a new axis.

**Commitment 8**: discipline-explainer document `devdocs/how_articulate_simple_should_be.md` §2.4 + §2.5 + §3 + §9 + §12.
- **Source**: the document itself.
- **Re-test status**:
  - §2.4: **CASCADE-FLAGGED for revision** (per Cascade A above; doc revisions are user-authorized COULDs below).
  - §2.5 (Rephrase): **CASCADE-DEEPENED** as Cascade B; not pre-decided here.
  - §3 (intra-discipline flow): MultiDepth's slot in Stage 3 is preserved structurally; the slot's content changes but the slot stays.
  - §9 (two-pass deferral): **CASCADE-DEEPENED** as Cascade C; not pre-decided here.
  - §12 (one-paragraph summary): **CASCADE-FLAGGED for revision** (per Cascade A above; the MultiDepth phrase needs updating).

## Next Actions

### MUST

(None proposed at this finding stage. The verdict's substantive content is the deliverable; specific text revisions wait on user authorization per the cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision pattern. Two cascade follow-up inquiries are flagged but not pre-decided.)

### COULD

- **What:** Apply Cascade A doc revisions to `devdocs/how_articulate_simple_should_be.md`. Specific text edits:
  1. **§2.4 essence sentence revision** (the load-bearing sentence at the top of §2.4 that names what MultiDepth does). Current text: "MultiDepth renders each item at two depths of meaning — the literal task, and the literal task wrapped in its perceived purpose chain." Proposed enhanced text: "MultiDepth renders each item's literal task and perceives the openness of its purpose chain (purpose-motivation ambiguities — the WHY axis; distinct from MQ3's intent-action ambiguities — the WHAT axis)." The enhancement operationalizes the AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction explicitly for the LLM.
  2. **§2.4 worked examples update.** Each worked example currently shows a purpose-wrapped output with causal connectives. Replace each purpose-wrapped output with identified-purpose-ambiguities format. For the cold-context shallow case (input *"rename foo to bar"*): preserve literal *"rename foo to bar"*; replace purpose-wrapped with explicit-empty *"No specific purpose-ambiguity perceivable from the task statement at cold context"*. For the substantive cold-context case (input *"add retries to the payment gateway call"*): preserve literal; replace purpose-wrapped with identified-purpose-ambiguities *"Purpose-motivation ambiguity: retries could be for transient network failures (most common engineering case), for timeout edge cases, for vendor SLA compliance, or for rate-limit handling. Without project context, multiple purposes are plausible."* For the warm-context case (input *"improve auth module"* with session context indicating token-validation discussion): preserve literal *"fix the token validation bug discussed"*; the warm-context substrate makes the purpose narrower but still ambiguous — identified-purpose-ambiguities along the same WHY axis.
  3. **§2.4 INCLUDES-with-accuracy rule scope refinement.** The rule's existing text covers purpose-wrapped's preservation of literal verbatim. Refine the scope explicitly: the INCLUDES rule applies to the literal output only (preserves input verbatim); the second output (identified-purpose-ambiguities) lists plausible purposes without wrapping the literal.
  4. **§2.4 substrate-compliance paragraph** stays unchanged. The paragraph already commits MultiDepth to the same substrate boundary as elsewhere in articulate; no text change needed.
  5. **§12 one-paragraph update.** Current phrase: "MultiDepth renders each item at literal + purpose-wrapped depths (the literal task, and the literal task included in its perceived purpose chain)." Replace with: "MultiDepth renders each item's literal task and perceives the openness of its purpose chain — emitting identified purpose-motivation ambiguities when openness is perceivable, or explicit-empty when no purpose-ambiguity is perceivable. Literal is preserved unchanged; only the purpose-perception output narrowed under the 23-18 refinement."
  6. **§11 inheritance map add a row** for this finding: a new row pointing to `devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-06_23-18__multidepth_purpose_wrapped_cascade_resolution/finding.md` with a short descriptive label, e.g., "MultiDepth purpose-wrapped narrowed to 2-shape {identified-purpose-ambiguities / explicit-empty} + LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT structural insight + AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction with MQ3."
  - **Who:** the user, when ready
  - **Gate:** observable trigger — user authorizes applying this finding's verdict to the doc
  - **Why:** brings the doc into alignment with the verdict; preserves cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision (Cascades B + C remain deferred).

- **What:** Apply the substantive update to the 22-44 finding (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-05_22-44__multiscope_depth_of_meaning_correction/finding.md`) and the 00-47 finding (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-06_00-47__multidepth_output_count_fixed_vs_variable/finding.md`). The 22-44 finding's "depth-of-meaning rendering" essence and the 00-47 finding's depth-carrier-via-connective-count commitment both need refinement acknowledgment when next consulted. Specific text additions:
  1. **22-44 finding** — add a "Refined by 23-18" note pointing to this finding's verdict.
  2. **00-47 finding** — add a "Refined by 23-18" note acknowledging the depth-carrier mechanism shifts from connective count to ambiguity-richness.
  - **Who:** the user, when ready
  - **Gate:** observable trigger — user authorizes applying refinement acknowledgments to prior findings
  - **Why:** keeps the prior findings' commitments aligned with this finding's refinement; prevents future readers from acting on outdated prior commitments without seeing the refinement.

### DEFERRED

- **What:** Resolve Cascade B — Rephrase's constraint source compounded. After this verdict, Rephrase (per §2.5 of the discipline-explainer document) has zero constraint sources at articulate-simple stage. Determine whether Rephrase emits ambiguity-spanning variants (one variant per plausible reading within each identified ambiguity from Meta-question + MultiDepth), or defers to articulate2 post-/surfacing where commitments exist, or is reconceived around ambiguity-shape constraints (varying across the ambiguity-space rather than within a committed frame).
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when the user is ready to address the Rephrase cascade; the cascade compounds two prior cascades (21-52 Cascade 2 + this finding's Cascade B), so its scope has grown.
  - **Why (if revived):** Rephrase is one of the five operations of articulate-simple; coherent operation definition requires resolution; the discipline-explainer document's §2.5 needs alignment.

- **What:** Resolve Cascade C — §9 two-pass deferral pressure. After this verdict, §9 of the discipline-explainer document commits articulate-simple as "complete on its own"; the substrate-bounded chain pressures this commitment further. Determine whether §9 refines to "complete as pre-context framing" (acknowledging articulate-simple's narrowed scope) or whether the two-pass design (articulate-simple → /surfacing → articulate2) is structurally necessary and reopened explicitly.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when the user is ready to address the §9 cascade; the cascade compounds two prior cascades (21-52 Cascade 3 + this finding's Cascade C).
  - **Why (if revived):** §9 commits the discipline's identity at the boundary; refinement has significant downstream implications for the project's cognitive loop structure.

- **What:** Test the **substrate-contamination-vs-downstream-bias** meta-pattern's transferability to a sibling upstream discipline (one whose output meaning-layer is being audited and whose downstream consumers lack the substrate the discipline operates under).
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when a sibling discipline's output meaning-layer comes under analysis with similar substrate-vs-downstream-consumers structure.
  - **Why (if revived):** the meta-pattern's transferability is currently evidenced at sample-size 1 (this case); additional positive transfers would strengthen the pattern's general claim; failed transfers would refine the pattern's preconditions.

- **What:** Test the **LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT** structural insight's transferability to other multi-output bundles. Specifically, audit each multi-output upstream-discipline bundle in the project's cognitive harness (e.g., any discipline that emits both an input-preservation and an additive-content output) and verify whether the literal-vs-additive structural distinction holds.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when other multi-output upstream-discipline bundles come under analysis.
  - **Why (if revived):** the insight enables surgical refinement; if it transfers, it becomes a reusable pattern; if a transfer fails (the "literal" output turned out to be a curated paraphrase that secretly committed), the pattern's precondition is sharpened.

## Reasoning

### Why the verdict was REFINE-only-purpose-wrapped (not PRESERVE, not DEFER, not HYBRID-context-conditional, not HYBRID-shape-split)

**PRESERVE** was the most natural defense — argue that MultiDepth's structural properties (INCLUDES + literal-fallback + perceivability + rendering-vs-committing + PATH-vs-ENDPOINT) make purpose-wrapped different in kind from Meta-question commitments and exempt it from the substrate-bounded chain. The defense fails because each structural property operates at a layer that doesn't reach the contamination layer (as articulated in the Finding above). PRESERVE was rejected on Correctness + USER-CLAIM-FIDELITY dimensions.

**DEFER-to-articulate2** would have eliminated purpose-wrapped from articulate-simple stage entirely; literal would be the only output at this stage; purpose-wrapped would emerge at the articulate2 stage after /surfacing has provided project context. DEFER is structurally coherent but premature relative to the user's question's scope. DEFER prejudges the §9 two-pass deferral cascade (Cascade 3 from the 21-52 finding, deepened here as Cascade C). The cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern from the 21-52 finding argues for not pre-deciding cascades. DEFER was rejected on SCOPE-MATCH dimension; the verdict respects the user's "lets dive deeper into this one" scope-bounding.

**HYBRID-context-conditional** would have made the verdict depend on cold-vs-warm context at runtime — warm context preserves purpose-wrapped (because session context provides substrate); cold context defers (because no substrate). The candidate fails because warm context provides session context, not project context — and the substrate-bounded chain's contamination concern is specifically about project context absence. Warm-context purpose-wrapped is still substrate-deficient relative to /surfacing's project-context. HYBRID-context-conditional was rejected on Correctness + SUBSTRATE-COMPLIANCE dimensions.

**HYBRID-shape-split** would have preserved literal at articulate-simple stage and refined purpose-wrapped specifically. This is structurally what REFINE-only-purpose-wrapped does. The two candidates effectively collapse — HYBRID-shape-split IS REFINE-only-purpose-wrapped when one recognizes that literal is non-contaminating per the LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT insight. The verdict adopts this label-collapsed form.

**REFINE-only-purpose-wrapped** is the surgical verdict: keep what doesn't need to change (literal output, MultiDepth's slot in the operation flow, the operation name); refine what does (the purpose-wrapped half's content shape). The verdict is consistent with the cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern (Cascades B + C named but not pre-decided). The verdict is consistent with USER-CLAIM-FIDELITY (engages the user's substrate-bounded argument structurally).

### Why the identity-collapse-with-MQ3 risk doesn't kill REFINE

A real concern arose: under refinement, both MultiDepth and MQ3 become ambiguity-identification operations; do they collapse into one? The 22-44 finding's PATH-vs-ENDPOINT distinction loses its surface form under refinement.

The distinction shifts to the AMBIGUITY-NATURE axis — MultiDepth at purpose-motivation (WHY); MQ3 at intent-action (WHAT). The distinction holds at the structural granularity in software-engineering vocabulary (purpose = motivation; intent = goal). The risk is at MED confidence because in colloquial use the two words sometimes conflate; the finding flags this for monitoring in Open Questions below.

### Why the §12 vs 21-52 runner-bias discrepancy doesn't kill the contamination case

The 21-52 Cascade 1 prose listed the runner as a downstream consumer of purpose-wrapped; §12 of the discipline-explainer document commits only Meta-question's MQ2 + MQ4 as runner reads. The discrepancy is real and acknowledged honestly (the finding flags the runner-bias claim from 21-52 as speculative pending §12 clarification).

The contamination case is robust without the runner-bias claim because two other downstream consumers are confirmed: Rephrase (per §1.1) and the user (per the user-verification role). Two confirmed consumers are sufficient grounding for the contamination case. The runner-bias claim's speculative status doesn't change the verdict; it just refines the finding's honesty about which downstream consumers are load-bearing.

### Why cascades are NAMED but not pre-decided

The 21-52 finding's **cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern** prevents two failure modes: (a) silent scope-creep — a verdict pre-deciding matters outside the user's question; (b) silent omission — structural consequences of the verdict not flagged. The honest pattern is to commit the substantive change in scope, name the cascades that follow structurally, and explicitly defer cascade-resolutions to follow-up inquiries.

The user's question was about Cascade 1 specifically ("lets dive deeper into this one"). Cascades B + C compound earlier cascades (Cascade B = 21-52 Cascade 2 deepened; Cascade C = 21-52 Cascade 3 deepened); their resolution scope has grown beyond what this finding's question covers. Each becomes its own follow-up.

### Why "transferability evidenced at sample-size 1" not "transferability confirmed"

The Critique discipline raised a language-strength concern about the substrate-contamination-vs-downstream-bias meta-pattern's transferability claim. The pattern is now transferred at one positive case (MultiDepth, this finding). One positive instance is positive evidence — but it's not universal confirmation. The finding uses the hedged language "evidenced at sample-size 1; broader cross-discipline test deferred" rather than "confirmed" to avoid overclaiming a single instance as a general result. Cross-discipline tests (per the DEFERRED Next Action) would strengthen the claim.

### Why LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT has a precondition

The pattern's correctness depends on the literal output being **genuine input-preservation**, not a curated paraphrase. The Critique discipline raised the failure case: a discipline whose "literal" output is in fact a curated paraphrase of the input would secretly commit to a perceived framing under the guise of preservation; the pattern would mis-apply. The precondition is named explicitly to prevent this misapplication.

For MultiDepth specifically, literal is "the task at its narrowest accurate framing" per §2.4 — narrowest accurate framing is genuine input-preservation when "accurate" is bounded to syntactic preservation of the task statement (which is what the §2.4 spec text indicates). The precondition holds at MultiDepth.

## Open Questions

### Monitoring

- **Cold-context conflation of purpose-ambiguity with intent-ambiguity.** The AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction (purpose-motivation = WHY axis; intent-action = WHAT axis) is structurally clean in software-engineering vocabulary but sometimes fuzzy in colloquial use. Observable telemetry: if Early Operation invocations (approximately 10-20 articulate-simple runs after the doc revisions land) show users systematically conflating MultiDepth's purpose-ambiguity outputs with MQ3's intent-ambiguity outputs (e.g., user-facing comments asking "isn't this the same as MQ3?", or downstream operations treating the two as interchangeable), the distinction needs explicit operationalization beyond the §2.4 essence-sentence enhancement.
- **LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT precondition stability.** Observable telemetry: if a sibling upstream discipline's "literal" output turns out to be a curated paraphrase (not genuine input-preservation) under analysis, the pattern's precondition needs sharpening with a determination mechanism for "genuine input-preservation."

### Blocked

- **Coherent definitional updates to articulate-simple at the discipline level.** Resolving Cascade B (§2.5 Rephrase constraint source) and Cascade C (§9 two-pass deferral) requires their own follow-up inquiries before the articulate-simple discipline's overall definition fully stabilizes. Until both cascades resolve, the discipline-explainer document's §2.5 + §9 carry potentially-stale commitments.

### Research Frontiers

- Whether the **substrate-contamination-vs-downstream-bias** meta-pattern applies to all upstream cognitive disciplines whose outputs feed downstream consumers without the substrate downstream needs, or whether discipline-specific properties affect its applicability. Cross-discipline tests would confirm or refine.
- Whether the **LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT** insight generalizes beyond multi-output bundles from substrate-bounded upstream disciplines (e.g., to multi-output bundles from any discipline; or to single-output preservation-vs-commitment distinctions within one discipline). Cross-discipline transfer would test the insight's structural scope.
- Whether the **surgical-refinement-within-multi-output-bundles** assembly pattern transfers reliably as a reusable approach for future cascade resolutions. The pattern is composed of three components (substrate-bounded chain transfer + AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction (where applicable) + LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT + cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision); whether all three are necessary for the pattern's effectiveness, or whether subsets suffice, is open.

### Refinement Triggers

- If user accepts this verdict and authorizes Cascade A doc revisions, the prior 22-44 + 00-47 findings' acknowledgment notes should also be applied (per the second COULD above).
- If a follow-up inquiry resolves Cascade B or Cascade C, this finding's verdict on PERMISSION scope (which extends to MultiDepth-at-articulate2-stage if articulate2 is structurally adopted) needs re-test against the resolved cascade.
- If Early Operation telemetry surfaces the AMBIGUITY-NATURE conflation in user-facing or downstream-discipline behavior, the §2.4 essence sentence enhancement may need further operationalization (e.g., explicit examples showing purpose vs intent at the same task).

This is a commitment — the LLM commits to a perceived purpose. Same substrate-bounded critique applies: without project context, the perceived purpose is a guess. Downstream consumers (the runner reading the purpose-wrapped to bias /surfacing toward the perceived purpose; the user reading the framing to verify it) act on the guessed purpose. # Finding: Rephrase's Constraint Source — Cascade 2 Resolution

## Changes from Prior

**Prior path:** `devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-06_23-18__multidepth_purpose_wrapped_cascade_resolution/finding.md` (referred to throughout as "the 23-18 finding"). The 23-18 finding directly named this cascade as "Cascade B" — Rephrase's constraint source compounded after the 21-52 finding (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-06_21-52__no_commitments_pre_surfacing_safety/finding.md`, the substrate-bounded + downstream-safety verdict) and the 23-18 finding both removed commitment-form constraints from Rephrase's input.

**Revision trigger:** Cascade 2 resolution. The user requested follow-up on Cascade 2 specifically ("okay lets dive deep into this one"). Cascade 2 names: Rephrase has zero commitment-form constraint sources at the articulate-simple stage after the two prior cascades. The "MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" — §2.5 of the discipline-explainer document `devdocs/how_articulate_simple_should_be.md` calls this "THE load-bearing safety mechanism of articulate" — no longer has its load-bearing input.

**What's preserved:**
- The 21-52 substrate-bounded chain (substrate-bounded ⇒ guess ⇒ downstream-bias-as-actionable ⇒ contamination) — confirmed transfers cleanly across cascade applications.
- The 21-52 scope-mismatch crux K2 (PERMISSION-not-CONSTRAINT operates at the LLM-emission scope; downstream-bias operates at the consumer scope; the layers don't connect) — preserved.
- The 21-52 substrate-contamination-vs-downstream-bias meta-pattern — transferability evidence now accumulates at sample-size 2 (after 23-18 + this finding). Language remains hedged ("evidence accumulating at sample-size 2") to avoid overclaim until broader cross-discipline tests provide more positive instances.
- The 21-52 cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern — REUSED consistently here.
- The 23-18 finding's LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT structural insight — extends in this finding to a broader pattern (see below).
- The 23-18 finding's AMBIGUITY-NATURE distinction (MultiDepth at WHY axis; MQ3 at WHAT axis) — preserved unchanged.
- All earlier prior commitments not specifically narrowed by this finding's verdict.

**What's changed:**
- **§2.5 of the discipline-explainer document** (the "Rephrase" section, which currently says "Rephrase produces alternative formulations of each item, constrained by the Meta-question answers" and names "the MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" as "THE load-bearing safety mechanism of articulate") is **REFINED**. Rephrase's essence shifts from "constrained by the Meta-question answers" to "spanning the plausible-readings of the same task within constraints from Deconstruct's deliverable-shape, the identified-ambiguities-list (from Meta-question + MultiDepth), Meta-question's NOT-list exclusions, and the substrate-bounded principle." The MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation refines to **multi-source-composition-constrains-Rephrase**.
- **The 04-07-48 finding** (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-04_07-48__task_define_process_layer/finding.md`, the source of §2.5's MQ-constrains-Rephrase commitment) is **REFINED**. The CLAIM STRUCTURE — that a load-bearing safety mechanism prevents Rephrase from locking the task into the wrong interpretive space — is preserved. The SOURCE-LIST of constraints providing the safety mechanism refines from MQ-only to multi-source-composition.
- **§2.5's vary-vocabulary-not-meaning principle** is **REFINED**. The principle's intent (Rephrase doesn't drift to a different task) is preserved. Its operational form refines to "Rephrase varies across plausible-readings of the same task; it does NOT drift to a different task." Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment from §2.3 provides the task-identity anchor that prevents drift.

**What's new:**
- A new structural insight (extension of the 23-18 LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT pattern): **VARIANT-SET-AS-OPENNESS-PRESERVATION**. Within a multi-output bundle from an upstream substrate-bounded discipline, a variant SET that spans the perceived ambiguity-space preserves the openness (analogous to how a literal output preserves the input); it carries no single commitment to a perceived property. Each individual variant is an exemplar of one plausible reading; the SET as a whole captures the openness. **Precondition** (load-bearing for pattern correctness): the variant-set must be bounded by openness-preservation (the ambiguity-space); the pattern does NOT apply to pure vocabulary variation without ambiguity-bound.
- A NEW meta-pattern: **constraint-source-disappearance-vs-operation-identity**. When an operation's load-bearing input is REMOVED by upstream substrate-bounded refinement (not just absent from initial design), the operation's identity can be preserved by recasting the input shape (commitment-form → ambiguity-form / multi-source-composition / variant-set form). The pattern names a structural move available when upstream cascades compound. **Precondition**: applies when load-bearing input is removed by upstream substrate-bounded refinement; not when input is absent from initial design.
- An **assembly emergent pattern**: **constraint-recasting-as-operation-preservation**. Components — substrate-bounded chain transferred to a new operation (this finding) + multi-source composition reframe + VARIANT-SET-AS-OPENNESS-PRESERVATION + constraint-source-disappearance-vs-operation-identity + cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision (carried from 21-52). This assembly EXTENDS the 23-18 surgical-refinement-within-multi-output-bundles pattern from output-content refinement to input-shape recasting.
- A previously-implicit observation now NAMED: **Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment was always one of Rephrase's constraints** per the doc line 290 (which says "Rephrase cannot change the task's deliverable type... This is one of the constraints Rephrase honors, alongside MQ1/MQ2/MQ3/MQ4/MQ-aggregate-resolution"). The §2.5 framing of "MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" as THE load-bearing safety mechanism understated the constraint set — Deconstruct's deliverable-shape was ALWAYS there. The refinement to multi-source-composition NAMES this structural reality explicitly.

**Migration:**
- §2.5 of the discipline-explainer document needs essence revision + load-bearing safety mechanism refinement + vary-vocabulary-not-meaning refinement per the COULDs below.
- §1.1 needs commitment refinement (Deconstruct deliverable-shape is binding; MultiDepth identified-purpose-ambiguities are an ambiguity-dimension).
- §13 worked examples C and D need updates to show variant-set form.
- §12 one-paragraph summary needs the Rephrase phrase refined.
- §11 inheritance map needs a new row.
- §4 NOT-list rule 3 stays unchanged — it actively supports the variant-set form ("emits multiple options").
- The 04-07-48 prior finding needs a refinement-acknowledgment note (the load-bearing safety mechanism claim refines to multi-source composition; claim structure preserved).
- The 19-17 prior finding (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-05_19-17__articulate_deconstruct_true_value/finding.md`, Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment) gets a REINFORCED note (Deconstruct's deliverable-shape role is now NAMED as one of the surviving constraint sources for Rephrase under the post-cascade state).
- Cascade C (§9 two-pass deferral pressure) compounds for the third time (21-52 + 23-18 + this finding); it remains DEFERRED per the cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision pattern. Each cascade follow-up has its own scope.

## Question

Given that the 21-52 finding narrowed Meta-question's permissive-answer range to 2-shape {identified-ambiguities / explicit-empty} (no commitments at articulate-simple stage) and the 23-18 finding narrowed MultiDepth's purpose-wrapped to 2-shape {identified-purpose-ambiguities / explicit-empty} (no commitments at articulate-simple stage) — and given that the combined result is Rephrase has zero commitment-form constraint sources at articulate-simple stage (the "MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" that §2.5 names "THE load-bearing safety mechanism of articulate" no longer has its load-bearing input) — what is Rephrase structurally under the post-cascade state: does it emit ambiguity-spanning variants (one variant per plausible reading), defer to articulate2 post-/surfacing, get reconceived around ambiguity-shape constraints, PRESERVE with surviving constraint sources, ELIMINATE entirely, or HYBRID?

**Goal**: a confident verdict naming the chosen candidate (or HYBRID) and engaging each rejected candidate on structural grounds. The verdict must name cascading implications (§2.5 + §1.1 + §13 + §12 + §11 + 04-07-48 + 19-17 + §9 Cascade C) honestly; pre-decide what's in scope; defer what's downstream per the cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern from 21-52 + 23-18.

## Finding Summary

- **The user's structural concern is correct.** Rephrase has zero commitment-form constraint sources at the articulate-simple stage after the 21-52 + 23-18 cascades. The "MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" — §2.5's named load-bearing safety mechanism — no longer has its load-bearing input. The structural pressure point is real.

- **But the load-bearing concern reframes.** §2.5's safety mechanism prevents "Rephrase from locking the task into the wrong interpretive space." Ambiguity-spanning variants — one variant per plausible reading within each identified ambiguity — KEEP the interpretive space OPEN. The variant SET as a whole prevents premature lock. This is structurally responsive to §2.5's load-bearing concern, not a violation of it.

- **The verdict is HYBRID-(a)+(d)**: Rephrase produces ambiguity-spanning variants WITHIN surviving constraint sources. The variants span the perceived ambiguity-space (one variant per plausible reading from Meta-question's identified-ambiguities + MultiDepth's identified-purpose-ambiguities). The surviving constraint sources compose multi-source: Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment (per §2.3 + the 19-17 finding), the identified-ambiguities-list itself (bounds dimensions), Meta-question's NOT-list exclusions, and the §1 substrate-bounded principle.

- **Multi-source composition reaches the load-bearing layer.** The composition is multiplicative-bound: deliverable-shape eliminates variants that change deliverable type; ambiguity-list bounds variation to perceived dimensions; NOT-list eliminates excluded vocabulary; substrate-bounded eliminates project-context drift. Together they reach §2.5's load-bearing layer. Realistic variant counts under typical cold context: 2-6 per item (well within manageable bounds; honors §2.5's "two or more rephrasings minimum" naturally).

- **MultiDepth identity preserved via three structural mechanisms.** First, §2.5's vary-vocabulary-not-meaning principle refines to "vary across plausible-readings of the same task; not drift to a different task" — Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment provides the task-identity anchor. Second, §4 NOT-list rule 3 (which explicitly says "It emits multiple options; the runner or the loop's first discipline acts on them") actively supports the variant-set form. Third, the operation-name "Rephrase" stays — "Rephrase" implies producing re-formulations; the variant-set form IS multiple re-formulations spanning plausible readings.

- **Five alternative candidates were tested and rejected on structural grounds**:
  - **(a) standalone**: combinatorial-explosion unbounded without (d)'s composition; rejected.
  - **(b) defer-to-articulate2**: prejudges §9 Cascade C (same critique 23-18 raised against MultiDepth DEFER); loses pre-context alternative-formulations value; rejected.

## Finding

### Context the reader needs

This finding sits inside an ongoing chain of refinements to a single cognitive discipline called **articulate_simple** — a five-operation discipline (Itemize / Meta-question / Deconstruct / MultiDepth / Rephrase) that takes a compact task statement and expands it into a per-item bundle the rest of the project's cognitive loop can work with. The discipline-explainer document for articulate_simple lives at `devdocs/how_articulate_simple_should_be.md`. It is referenced throughout this finding by section number (§1, §2.5, §3, etc.).

The discipline is committed to **substrate-bounded operation** per §1 of the doc — it does not fetch project files, read recent inquiry history, or load specific artifacts. The substrate is the task statement plus the LLM's general knowledge plus any session context already loaded.

Two prior findings narrowed the discipline's commitments at the articulate-simple stage:

- The **21-52 finding** (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-06_21-52__no_commitments_pre_surfacing_safety/finding.md`) established that any commitment the LLM makes at the articulate-simple stage is a guess (no project context to ground it on) and that downstream consumers act on the guess as actionable framing. It narrowed Meta-question's permissive-answer range from four shapes (identified-ambiguity / confident commitment / hedged commitment / explicit-empty) to two shapes (identified-ambiguity / explicit-empty).

- The **23-18 finding** (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-06_23-18__multidepth_purpose_wrapped_cascade_resolution/finding.md`) extended the same substrate-bounded chain to MultiDepth's purpose-wrapped output, narrowing it from a committed-purpose-chain to two shapes (identified-purpose-ambiguities / explicit-empty). It also surfaced the LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT structural insight: input-preservation outputs in a multi-output bundle are non-contaminating.

The 23-18 finding flagged THREE follow-up cascades from its verdict. **Cascade B** named: §2.5 of the doc commits "the MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" as "THE load-bearing safety mechanism of articulate"; with MQ commitments removed (by the 21-52 finding) AND MultiDepth's purpose-wrapped commitments removed (by the 23-18 finding), Rephrase has zero commitment-form constraint sources at the articulate-simple stage. This finding resolves that cascade. (For continuity with the user's named candidates, the cascade is referred to throughout as **Cascade 2** — the same cascade the 21-52 finding originally flagged as "Cascade 2: Rephrase's constraint source disappears.")

The user's request, verbatim: *"Cascade 2 — Rephrase's constraint source: under §2.5, Rephrase produces alternative formulations of each item 'constrained by the Meta-question answers.' Under this verdict, MQ answers carry no commitments — only identified-ambiguities or explicit-empty. Rephrase's constraint source disappears. Follow-up inquiry needed to determine whether Rephrase under verdict (a) emits ambiguity-spanning variants (one variant per plausible reading within each identified ambiguity), (b) defers to articulate2 post-/surfacing where Rephrase has commitments to constrain on, or (c) is reconceived around ambiguity-shape constraints (varying across the ambiguity-space rather than within a committed frame). okay lets dive deep into this one."*

### What Rephrase currently commits to (background)

Under the current §2.5 of the discipline-explainer document, Rephrase is committed as follows:

- **Essence**: "Rephrase produces alternative formulations of each item, constrained by the Meta-question answers."
- **Vary-vocabulary-not-meaning principle**: "Rephrase varies vocabulary, emphasis, and what's implicit-vs-explicit. It does NOT vary meaning — the constraint imposed by the Meta-question answers (plus MQ-aggregate-resolution's output) is what keeps Rephrase from drifting."
- **Load-bearing safety mechanism claim**: "The MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation is THE load-bearing safety mechanism of articulate. Without it, Rephrase would tend to expand each item along whatever vocabulary the LLM finds salient, which often locks the task into the wrong interpretive space."
- **Positive description**: "With it, Rephrase explores alternative formulations within the perceived scope (MQ1), the perceived context-need + stance (MQ2), the perceived intent (MQ3), and the perceived coherence (MQ-aggregate-resolution)."
- **Minimum**: "Two or more rephrasings per item is the minimum."
- **Source**: 04-07-48 finding (`devdocs/inquiries/2026-06-04_07-48__task_define_process_layer/finding.md`).

The doc also commits at §1.1: "Deconstruct and MultiDepth's outputs are additional structure to vary along" — Rephrase reads both Meta-question's answers AND Deconstruct's + MultiDepth's outputs as input. Deconstruct's §2.3 paragraph (line 290 of the doc) further commits: "Rephrase cannot change the task's deliverable type... This is one of the constraints Rephrase honors, alongside MQ1/MQ2/MQ3/MQ4/MQ-aggregate-resolution."

The constraint set, in other words, was always multi-source. §2.5's framing of "MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" as THE load-bearing safety mechanism was an over-statement — Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment was always part of the constraint set, just not named in §2.5's load-bearing claim. The 21-52 + 23-18 cascades have made this structural reality visible: the load-bearing safety mechanism isn't a single relation; it's a composition of multiple constraint sources.

### The user's concern is structurally correct

After the 21-52 + 23-18 cascades, Rephrase has zero commitment-form constraint sources at the articulate-simple stage. Meta-question's answers are identified-ambiguities (no commitments to perceived properties). MultiDepth's second output is identified-purpose-ambiguities (no commitments to perceived purpose). The constraint shape the §2.5 load-bearing claim depended on is gone.

But three other constraint sources remain. Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment (per §2.3 + the 19-17 finding) is preserved — Deconstruct's commitments are structural facts about the task (what kind of deliverable is asked for), not perceived properties of the task; substrate-bounded contamination doesn't apply. Meta-question's NOT-list exclusions (MQ4) are preserved in identified-exclusion-ambiguity form. The §1 substrate-bounded principle is preserved. These three plus the identified-ambiguities-list shape itself compose a multi-source constraint set.

### The structural reframe of the load-bearing concern

§2.5's named failure mode — what the safety mechanism is supposed to prevent — is Rephrase "locking the task into the wrong interpretive space." This is a NEGATIVE constraint (prevent premature lock), not a POSITIVE constraint (drive variation toward).

Ambiguity-spanning variants — one variant per plausible reading within each identified ambiguity — KEEP the interpretive space OPEN. The variant SET as a whole represents multiple plausible readings; no single reading is committed to. The reader (the user, the runner formulating /surfacing's input, the loop's first discipline) sees the openness explicitly; the loop's downstream operations (with substrate) can adjudicate among readings later.

This is the substrate-respecting form of §2.5's load-bearing safety mechanism. It is RESPONSIVE to the failure mode §2.5 names, not violating of it.

### The verdict — HYBRID-(a)+(d)

Under the verdict, Rephrase at the articulate-simple stage produces:

- **Alternative formulations of each item**, where the formulations are emitted as **ambiguity-spanning variants** — one variant per plausible reading within each identified ambiguity.
- The plausible readings come from Meta-question's identified-ambiguities (now under 21-52's narrowing) plus MultiDepth's identified-purpose-ambiguities (now under 23-18's narrowing).
- The variants are **bounded** by a multi-source constraint composition:
  1. **Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment** — variants preserve the task's deliverable type; rephrasings that change deliverable type (e.g., turning "write a report" into "build a system") are excluded.
  2. **The identified-ambiguities-list itself** — variants vary along dimensions perceived as open; variants don't vary along dimensions where the LLM perceives no ambiguity.
  3. **Meta-question's NOT-list exclusions (MQ4)** — variants don't include excluded vocabulary or framings.
  4. **The §1 substrate-bounded principle** — variants don't include project-specific terms not in session context.

The variant slot in the per-item bundle is preserved. Stage 4 of the intra-discipline flow (per §3) stays — Rephrase still runs last; its constraint set has refined shape.

The "MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" refines to **multi-source-composition-constrains-Rephrase**. §2.5's vary-vocabulary-not-meaning principle refines to "Rephrase varies across plausible-readings of the same task; it does NOT drift to a different task." Deconstruct's deliverable-shape commitment provides the task-identity anchor that prevents drift.

§2.5's "Two or more rephrasings per item is the minimum" is preserved naturally — the variant-set typically contains 2-6 rephrasings per item under realistic cold-context conditions.

§4 NOT-list rule 3 — which says explicitly "It emits multiple options... the runner or the loop's first discipline acts on them" — stays unchanged. It actively supports the variant-set form.

### Why the verdict is surgical, not blanket

A blanket refinement might have eliminated Rephrase from the articulate-simple stage entirely (the (b) DEFER candidate) or removed it as structurally redundant (the (e) ELIMINATE candidate). We didn't, for two structural reasons.

First, (b) DEFER prejudges Cascade C. The 23-18 finding raised this critique against MultiDepth DEFER: eliminating an operation from the articulate-simple stage forces structural reconception of §9's two-pass design before that resolution is in scope. The cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern argues for verdicts that PRESERVE the affected cascade as deferred. (b) violates this pattern. (b) also loses pre-context alternative-formulations value — the user reads the per-item bundle for framing verification; the runner reads it to formulate /surfacing's input. Both consumers benefit from the variant-set at the pre-context stage.

Second, (e) ELIMINATE loses §2.5's "alternative formulations" commitment entirely. Rephrase has intrinsic value beyond the load-bearing safety mechanism claim — the plurality of expression for the same task helps the user and the runner see alternative readings of an ambiguous task statement. Eliminating loses that plurality without a structural insight that compensates.

The (c) ambiguity-shape-constraints candidate is structurally interesting but collapses into (a) at the operational level. "Varying across ambiguity-shape" requires either (i) emitting one variant per ambiguity type — which IS (a) — or (ii) emitting variants without specifying how many or what content — which has no operational bound and collapses to pure vocabulary variation without constraint, the exact failure mode §2.5 warns about. (c) as standalone is ill-defined.

The (a) standalone candidate has a combinatorial-explosion risk: 3 MQ1 ambiguities × 4 MQ2 × 2 MQ3 × MultiDepth ambiguities = potentially many variants per item. The (d) standalone candidate provides bounds but no operational form for variation. HYBRID-(a)+(d) addresses both: variants span the ambiguity-space WITHIN the multi-source composition's bounds. Realistic variant counts under typical cold context are 2-6 per item (most ambiguities will be explicit-empty in cold context per the 18-21 finding's empty-as-content principle inherited via §2.4's perceivability rule).

### Why the load-bearing concern reframes

The structural insight that makes the verdict work: §2.5's "load-bearing safety mechanism" is a NEGATIVE constraint, not a POSITIVE one. It prevents drift; it doesn't drive variation toward a committed frame.

NEGATIVE constraints can be served by BOUNDS without requiring commitment-form input. The multi-source composition (Deconstruct deliverable-shape + ambiguity-list + MQ4 NOT-list + substrate-bounded) provides BOUNDS at different layers:
- Deconstruct deliverable-shape bounds the deliverable TYPE
- Ambiguity-list bounds the variation DIMENSIONS
- MQ4 NOT-list bounds the VOCABULARY
- Substrate-bounded bounds the SUBSTRATE

Together these reach the load-bearing layer §2.5 originally named — preventing Rephrase from "expanding along whatever vocabulary the LLM finds salient." The composition is multiplicative-bound: each source eliminates a region of variant-space.

The §2.5 framing of "MQ-constrains-Rephrase relation" as the safety mechanism over-stated the role of MQ commitments. The actual structural mechanism was always multi-source — Deconstruct's deliverable-shape was always in the constraint set per line 290 of the doc. The 21-52 + 23-18 cascades have made this visible by removing the MQ-commitment piece and forcing the multi-source composition into the foreground.

### How identity is preserved

The 19-06 finding's asymmetric-naming-implies-output-identity meta-pattern: an operation's name implies its output identity. "Rephrase" implies producing re-formulations. Under the verdict, Rephrase produces re-formulations spanning the ambiguity-space — multiple alternative formulations of the same task at the per-item level. The name preserves its structural meaning. The user has the final call on the operation name per the 19-06 + 20-29 + 23-18 chain of name-preservation decisions; this finding doesn't propose a rename.

The 23-18 finding's LITERAL-AS-NON-CONTAMINATING-OUTPUT structural insight extends here to a broader pattern: **VARIANT-SET-AS-OPENNESS-PRESERVATION**. Within a multi-output bundle from an upstream substrate-bounded discipline, an output that preserves the input verbatim (like MultiDepth's literal output post-23-18) AND an output that preserves the openness via a variant-set (like Rephrase's variant-set under this verdict) are BOTH non-contaminating. The contamination locus is single-commitment outputs that ADD perceived content based on guess.

The pattern's PRECONDITION is load-bearing: the variant-set must be bounded by openness-preservation (the ambiguity-space). Pure vocabulary variation without ambiguity-bound would NOT qualify — there's no openness being preserved if the variation isn't tied to perceived ambiguities. The precondition is what distinguishes the safe form (variants spanning the ambiguity-space) from the failure mode §2.5 warns about (variants expanding along whatever vocabulary the LLM finds salient).

### The constraint-source-disappearance-vs-operation-identity new meta-pattern

This finding surfaces a NEW meta-pattern: **constraint-source-disappearance-vs-operation-identity**. When an operation's load-bearing input is REMOVED by upstream substrate-bounded refinement (not just absent from initial design), the operation's identity can be preserved by recasting the input shape. The recasting moves the operation from depending on commitment-form input to depending on ambiguity-form / multi-source-composition / variant-set form input.

The PRECONDITION is load-bearing: the pattern applies when input is REMOVED by upstream refinement (the input was present in a prior version of the design and got narrowed away by a cascade); it does NOT apply when input is absent from initial design (in which case the operation may simply not be viable, or the operation may need a different structural resolution).

The pattern names a structural move available when upstream cascades compound. It generalizes a structural strategy that's been implicit in the iterative refinement chain (18-21 → 19-06 → 20-29 → 21-52 → 23-18 → this finding) but wasn't named until this finding's analysis. Whether the pattern transfers to operations beyond Rephrase is a Research Frontier (see Open Questions below).

### Three structural items named honestly without pre-decision

The verdict's substantive scope is bounded to the Rephrase constraint-source resolution. Three structural items follow; this finding names them honestly per the 21-52 cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern.

**Cascade A — immediate doc + prior finding revisions.** §2.5 essence sentence + load-bearing safety mechanism refinement + vary-vocabulary-not-meaning principle refinement; §1.1 commitment refinement; §13 worked examples C and D updates; §12 one-paragraph update; §11 inheritance map row addition. Plus the 04-07-48 prior finding refinement-acknowledgment note (claim structure preserved; source-list refined) and the 19-17 prior finding REINFORCED note (Deconstruct deliverable-shape is now NAMED as one of the surviving constraint sources). This finding's substantive deliverable. User-authorized via the COULDs below.

**Cascade C — §9 two-pass deferral pressure compounded for the third time.** The 21-52 finding deepened §9's "complete on its own" commitment pressure; the 23-18 finding deepened it further; this finding deepens it again. The cumulative pressure is significant. But per the cascade-acknowledgment-without-pre-decision meta-pattern, the specific resolution of §9 is NOT pre-decided here. The follow-up Cascade C inquiry will address whether §9 refines to "complete as pre-context framing" or whether the two-pass design (articulate-simple → /surfacing → articulate2) is structurally reopened.

**§3 Stage 4 preservation accounting (NOT a cascade in the pressure-carrying sense; preservation note).** §3 Stage 4 sequence is preserved — Rephrase still runs last in the per-item flow; the refined constraint set flows through. This is preservation, not cascade — it doesn't carry forward structural pressure the way Cascade C does. We name it here for completeness of the post-verdict accounting; downstream readers can verify that §3's Stage 4 commitment is undisturbed.
