# Finding: Paper 13 (Nemeth et al. 2004, Using Cognitive Artifacts to Understand Distributed Cognition) — breakthrough or not?

## Question

The literal ask: *"dive deep into `devdocs/paper_seed/13.md` — breakthrough or not?"*

This is the latest dive in an ongoing **paper-harvest** — a series that takes one academic paper at a time and asks a single disciplined question: *does this paper hand us a genuinely new way to think or work (a "breakthrough"), or does it merely confirm and sharpen what our project already has?* The harvest judges every paper by one fixed gate, **the import test**: an insight counts as a real import only if it either (a) **NAMES** something we already do but had never named, or (b) **RESOLVES** a confusion that genuinely pre-existed. Anything else is **confirming** (agrees with us without adding). A "breakthrough" specifically means a **new frame or a new practice** — not the sharpening or relabeling of an existing one.

Paper 13 is Nemeth, Cook, O'Connor, and Klock (2004), "Using Cognitive Artifacts to Understand Distributed Cognition." It is a human-factors field study of anesthesia coordinators in a hospital operating-room suite, who plan and manage staff-to-procedure assignments under time pressure using **cognitive artifacts** — schedules, boards, worksheets that a team shares to coordinate. It is the most on-topic paper the harvest has met: we *are* a system whose memory lives in external cognitive artifacts (our canon documents, findings, route-maps). Its genre is design/human-factors — closer to our own work than any prior paper — which is exactly why it needed a careful hearing rather than a quick dismissal.

## Finding Summary

- **Verdict: NOT a breakthrough.** Paper 13 is **confirming-plus at the higher end** of the harvest — the closest-to-us paper so far. It confirms and mildly sharpens our existing frame; it does not deliver a new frame or a new practice.

- **The one genuine residue is the artifact quality-criteria set** — the paper's claim that any cognitive artifact "must be accurate, efficient, reliable, informative, clear, and malleable" (plus a value-add layer: prompting, speculation, consequences, value-based decisions). This is a **mild organizing contribution**: it collects into one named checklist the artifact-quality standards we already hold, but hold **scattered** across several places.

- **A load-bearing correction came out of the review.** The dive initially framed the criteria as "decomposing our single blurry *Sustained* bar." Verification against canon showed that's wrong: **"Sustained" is not a standalone artifact-trust bar** — it is the first word of our era-goal SUSTRALL, a four-part quality bar. The criteria don't decompose one bar; they **aggregate several scattered commitments** (see the Finding). The verdict holds; the framing is corrected and is now more honest.

- **The distinctive yield is method-level, not content.** Two results for the harvest itself: (1) paper 13 is the **first live validation** of a standing method-flag (that our "confirming-plus flavor" vocabulary risks over-proliferating) — the flag correctly declined to mint a new flavor here; (2) it **generalizes a prior diagnostic pattern** with a genre-match axis (below), provisionally.

- **The reverse-lens bounds what transfers.** The paper's cognition is distributed **socially** (a team sharing artifacts in real time); ours is distributed **temporally** (one cognizer across sessions). So the through-time part transfers cleanly; the across-people part largely does not.

- **The absorptive frame held.** This is the 8th consecutive paper whose transferable residue maps *into* our existing memory frame (**grasp-management**) as confirming-plus rather than breaching it.

## Finding

### The frame this verdict operates under

Two opposite failure modes shadow a dive this on-topic. One is **manufacturing** a breakthrough because the paper resonates — it is a study of designing cognitive artifacts, and we design cognitive artifacts, so it is tempting to over-credit the closeness. The other is **reflexively dismissing** it because its subject is hospital scheduling and patient safety — grading its substrate down for the genre. The import test avoids both: it asks only whether the paper names something unnamed or resolves a real prior confusion, regardless of how close or far the surface looks. The verdict below was earned against both pulls.

### The one genuine residue: the artifact quality-criteria set

The paper's sharpest content is a set of standards every cognitive artifact must meet. Quoted: *"any cognitive artifact in this environment, whether paper or computer-supported, must be accurate, efficient, reliable, informative, clear, and malleable"* — each defined operationally (accurate = "current and valid in its representation of the system state"; efficient = "impose the least burden on users to obtain information"; informative = not a "keyhole view" that "prevent[s] practitioners from making connections"; and so on). Plus a forward-looking value-add layer: prompting (*"survey information… for gaps and inconsistencies… nominate such item(s)"*), speculation, consequences, and value-based decisions (*"templates… capture… expertise and make it available for use by others"*).

This is strikingly on our topic: it is about a downstream reader *using* an artifact — exactly our concern that a later session must be able to pick up and trust a finding. So we tested it at full force, including the inversion *"it IS a breakthrough — this is the operational usability frame we lacked."*

It does not clear the bar, and the reason is that **each criterion maps to a commitment we already hold**:

- *accurate* ↔ our finding **status frontmatter** (`status: active` / `supersedes:` / `refines:`) — findings carry their own currency/validity;
- *efficient* and *clear* ↔ our **write-for-cold-reader** rule (the concluding step's instruction to *"write for a reader who has NOT seen the discipline outputs"* and to be *"complete but not dense"*);
- *informative* (not a keyhole) ↔ our **quality test** (that a reader can *"read ONLY finding.md… and understand the complete decision"*) plus the Reasoning and Open Questions sections that give the reader the full field, not just one answer;
- *reliable* ↔ our findings' persistence as external files (available when a later session needs them);
- *malleable* ↔ **cultivated-not-found** (a prior harvest result: our artifacts are authored and edited by the same system that reads them).

Each individually is confirming. The **only** novelty is the *aggregation* — collecting these into one named checklist. Collecting things we already track into a single list is a genuine but **mild organizing contribution**, not a new capability. And because it would **refine an existing grading practice** (we already grade findings for usability, via the quality test) rather than introduce a new one, it is a **regulative import** — credited honestly, a regulative import is not lesser — but not a **new practice**, so not a breakthrough. This is the load-bearing line: **refines-not-adds**. Even granting the strongest reading (that a six-criteria checklist is genuinely more discriminating than one blurry "is this usable?" judgment, and could catch a clear-but-not-informative finding), it *sharpens how we make an existing decision* rather than adding a new decision or a new frame.

### The correction: "Sustained" is not a standalone artifact-trust bar

The dive's early framing said the criteria "decompose our single blurry *Sustained* bar." The review checked "Sustained" against canon and found the framing over-specified. **"Sustained" is the first word of SUSTRALL** (our era-goal, the SUStained TRAversal Loop of Loops), and canon defines it as a *four-part* quality bar — the loop must be worth keeping in motion: *"turns are low-friction, artifacts are trustworthy (checkable, resumable), interruption is graceful, and outputs are wanted"* (`docs/canon/sustained_traversal_loop_of_loops.md`). So "artifacts are trustworthy" is a real, named commitment — but it is *one of four* under Sustained, not a standalone "Sustained artifact-trust bar."

The honest re-grounding: the criteria-set aggregates commitments that are genuinely **scattered** — SUSTRALL's "trustworthy artifacts" commitment, plus write-for-cold-reader, plus the quality test, plus status frontmatter, plus cultivated-not-found — living across canon, the concluding protocol, and finding frontmatter. This makes the organizing story slightly *stronger* (aggregating scattered commitments is more useful than tidying one bar), while leaving the verdict exactly where it was: confirming-plus, not a breakthrough. The correction is recorded plainly because the over-specification entered this dive's own working vocabulary and verification caught it — the harvest's discipline is to verify canon terms before building on them, not to assert them.

### The characteristic shape, and the confirmations

Paper 13's shape differs from the prior dive's (paper 14, an extended-mind philosophy paper). That paper's distinctive content was bracketed metaphysics that didn't transfer, so its value flipped to a *mirror* (clarifying our disanalogies). Paper 13, being a **right-genre design paper**, instead yields **source content** (the criteria) that transfers — but the source *confirms and organizes* rather than introducing anything new. In effect paper 13 delivers the functional/design content that the paper-14 finding said was "the more-transferable half" it only gestured at — and it lands as confirming-organizing.

Two further maps confirm (do not extend) existing commitments:
- **The coordinator as allocator.** The anesthesia coordinator allocates a scarce resource (staff) against demand under uncertainty, mediated by an artifact (the schedule), *"striv[ing] to reduce the degree of uncertainty to a manageable set."* This rhymes with our **orchestrator's** allocator-shape (allocating attention over a route-field). It is a confirming worked-example, not an import — and the disanalogy is real (a human domain-expert assigning staff in real time is not the same as an attention-allocator across sessions).
- **The plan→log lifecycle.** The paper notes an artifact *"evolv[es] from a plan of procedures… into a log of procedures that have been performed."* That confirms what our route-map plus its done/explored column already do.

### What does not transfer (the quarantine)

Applying the reverse-lens — separating what's true of a real-time human team from what transfers to our single-system, across-sessions, external-file architecture:

- **The healthcare / patient-safety superstructure** — the paper's actual purpose. We have no care, morbidity, or mortality stakes. Non-transferable.
- **The paper-vs-computer polemic** (that a digital artifact merely mimicking a paper one is "blind to the… refined interactions") — the specific claim doesn't transfer (we have no paper artifacts). Two residues survive: the computer's concrete failures (a "keyhole view," four-menu drill-downs, truncated descriptions) *reinforce* why the criteria matter; and "understand the work first, then build" is a mild design lesson.
- **The social distribution.** This is the key disanalogy. The paper's cognition is distributed **across people** in real time (many cognizers sharing one live board). Ours is distributed **across time** (the products of earlier sessions transform later ones — one cognizer, many sessions). So distribution-through-time maps in cleanly (it is our cross-run memory); distribution-across-people is a stretch and is quarantined.

### Where this sits in the harvest

This is the **8th consecutive paper** whose transferable residue maps into **grasp-management** (our canonized frame: memory lives in external files; *grasp* is the fraction a session holds live, *reach* is what it can look up but isn't holding) as confirming-plus, rather than breaching it. The frame absorbed the closest-to-us paper without strain.

## Inherited Commitments Re-test

This inquiry's `_branch.md` declared a Synthesis Trigger — it tests paper 13 against standing commitments. Each is re-tested with evidence.

- **Commitment: the import test discriminates.**
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — commitment confirmed. It did real work both ways: it **passed** the criteria-set as a mild organizing residue *without* inflating it to breakthrough, and it **failed** the healthcare thesis and the paper-vs-computer specific claim. A gate that discriminates both ways on the closest-to-us paper is doing its job.

- **Commitment: `docs/canon/grasp_management.md`** (reach≠grasp; external memory) is the absorptive frame.
  - **Source:** `docs/canon/grasp_management.md`.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — commitment confirmed. Paper 13's substrate mapped *in* as confirming-plus; the criteria-set sits inside the frame (artifact-quality within external memory) without breaching it. n=8.

- **Commitment: the reverse-lens** (quarantine what's true of the human setting before grading).
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — commitment confirmed. It quarantined the healthcare superstructure and the paper-vs-computer claim precisely, and it produced the load-bearing **social-vs-temporal** disanalogy that bounds the transfer.

- **Commitment: the "Sustained" artifact-trust bar / write-for-cold-reader / the orchestrator** (the mapping targets).
  - **Source:** `docs/canon/sustained_traversal_loop_of_loops.md`; the concluding protocol's quality test + write-for-cold-reader rule; the worker/navigation/orchestrator split.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — **commitment confirmed but frame CORRECTED.** Verification showed "Sustained" is SUSTRALL's four-part worth-keeping-in-motion bar, **not** a standalone artifact-trust bar as the dive initially framed it. The criteria-set aggregates SUSTRALL's "trustworthy artifacts" commitment plus write-for-cold-reader plus the quality test plus status frontmatter (scattered). The coordinator confirms the orchestrator's allocator-shape (an illustration, not an extension). The correction is recorded as an anti-confabulation catch.

- **Commitment: the confirming-plus flavor category** (four flavors + a prior sub-flavor).
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame + the `harvest-flavor-proliferation-flag` memory.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — commitment confirmed, and the flag **validated**. Paper 13 was a candidate to mint a "criteria-namer" flavor; the decision-vs-label test (does the flavor change a decision, or only a label?) said *label* → declined. This is the flag's first live test, and it worked.

## Next Actions

Nothing here is required — the finding is a verdict, and a confirming-plus verdict opens optional sharpenings, not obligations. Captured from the dive's route-map (`routelister.md`).

### COULD

- **Aggregate the scattered artifact-quality commitments into one usability checklist.**
  - **What:** collect SUSTRALL's "trustworthy artifacts (checkable, resumable)" + write-for-cold-reader + the quality test + status frontmatter + cultivated-not-found into a single named checklist a finding-author/grader can consult; paper 13's six criteria (accurate/efficient/reliable/informative/clear/malleable) are candidate headers.
  - **Who:** a future canon or concluding-protocol pass (user-gated).
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when next editing the concluding quality test or authoring an artifact-quality note.
  - **Why:** one place instead of five scattered commitments; refines *how* the existing usability-grading practice is applied. This is the dive's most actionable content-yield — but it is a refinement (aggregate what exists), not a new gate.

- **Record the "Sustained" correction as canon-hygiene.**
  - **What:** note that "Sustained" is SUSTRALL's four-part quality bar, not a standalone artifact-trust bar, so future dives don't re-confabulate a single "Sustained bar."
  - **Gate:** observable — if the harvest again reaches for "the Sustained bar" as one artifact-quality criterion.
  - **Why:** the over-specification entered this session's own framing; recording the correction prevents recurrence.

### DEFERRED

- **Promote (or drop) the genre-match diagnostic shape.**
  - **What:** the pattern "a maximally on-topic paper's yield depends on genre-match — a right-genre (design) paper yields *source* content that confirms/organizes; a wrong-genre (philosophy) paper flips to *mirror*." It generalizes the prior dive's source→mirror observation with a genre axis.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — promote if a 3rd maximally-on-topic paper fits the split. Carry the named confound: paper 13's operational/design-native character could drive "source content" independently of genre-match, so n=2 is suggestive, not established.
  - **Why (if revived):** a cheap predictor of a maximally-on-topic paper's yield-*type* before diving.

- **Settle the confirming-plus flavor taxonomy.**
  - **What:** with the flag now validated once (this dive) and flagged once before, decide whether "confirming-plus" alone should carry the grade going forward, dropping per-paper flavors.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — one more decline (a next paper where a flavor is declined) would settle it.
  - **Why (if revived):** prevents the grading vocabulary from becoming a labeling exercise.

## Reasoning

The verdict is **NOT a breakthrough / confirming-plus (higher end)**, stress-tested rather than assumed:

- **The it-IS-a-breakthrough inversion** ("the criteria-set is the operational usability frame we lacked") — **rejected**, after a genuine hearing. Defeated three ways: each criterion maps to a named commitment (content confirming); the only novelty is the aggregation (organizing, not generative); it refines an existing grading practice (refines-not-adds). This was the anti-manufacture guard doing its work on the closest-to-us paper.

- **The aggregation-is-itself-the-import inversion** ("a six-criteria checklist genuinely changes the grading decision") — **granted, and it sharpened rather than broke the verdict.** Even granting the checklist is more discriminating, the decision it changes is the *existing* "is this usable?" decision; it sharpens how we make that decision rather than adding a new one. The verdict came to rest on **refines-not-adds**, which holds even when the checklist's operational force is granted.

- **The "Sustained bar" framing** — **corrected, not defended.** Verification against canon showed "Sustained" is SUSTRALL's four-part bar, not a standalone artifact-trust criterion. Rather than protect the neat "decomposes one bar" story, the finding adopts the honest "aggregates scattered commitments" story — which happens to be a slightly stronger organizing account. This is the anti-confabulation discipline: verify canon terms, don't assert them.

- **The emergent's confound** — **named, not hidden.** The genre-match pattern is real but provisional at two data points, and paper 13's design-native character is a plausible alternative driver of its "source content." Kept deferred with the confound stated.

- **What survived:** the verdict; the criteria-set as a mild organizing residue (with the corrected aggregates-scattered framing); the two method-yields (flag validated; genre-match provisional); the precise quarantine. No candidate for a genuine new frame or practice survived — because none was there.

The through-line was **non-sycophancy in four directions**: don't inflate the closest-to-us paper (anti-manufacture); don't dismiss its operational criteria for the healthcare genre (anti-overcorrection); don't over-promote the two-point emergent (anti-inflation); and don't build on an unverified canon term (anti-confabulation).

## Open Questions

### Monitoring
- Whether **grasp-management** keeps absorbing on-topic papers as confirming-plus. Observable across the remaining harvest.

### Refinement Triggers
- **The genre-match diagnostic shape is promoted** if a 3rd maximally-on-topic paper fits the right-genre→source / wrong-genre→mirror split (confound permitting).
- **The confirming-plus taxonomy is settled** at the next paper where a flavor is declined — one more decline argues for collapsing to plain confirming-plus.
- **The artifact-usability checklist (COULD) is acted on** only when the concluding quality test or an artifact-quality note is next edited.

# Finding: Paper 12 (Enfield 2005, The Body as a Cognitive Artifact in Lao Kinship Gesture) — breakthrough or not?

## Question

The literal ask: *"dive deep into `devdocs/paper_seed/12.md` — breakthrough or not?"*

This is the latest dive in an ongoing **paper-harvest** — a series that takes one academic paper at a time and asks a single disciplined question: *does this paper hand us a genuinely new way to think or work (a "breakthrough"), or does it only confirm and sharpen what our project already has?* The harvest judges every paper by one fixed gate, **the import test**: an insight counts as a real import only if it either (a) **NAMES** something we already do but had never named, or (b) **RESOLVES** a confusion that genuinely pre-existed. Anything else is **confirming** (agrees with us without adding). A "breakthrough" specifically means a **new frame or a new practice** — not the sharpening or relabeling of an existing one.

Paper 12 is N. J. Enfield (2005), "The Body as a Cognitive Artifact in Kinship Representations: Hand Gesture Diagrams by Speakers of Lao" (*Current Anthropology*). It is a linguistic-anthropology field study: Lao speakers, asked to explain their kinship system, spontaneously "draw" kinship diagrams in mid-air with their hands — assigning relatives to chunks of empty space and pointing back to those spots. Enfield's claim is that the body (co-speech hand gesture) is a **cognitive artifact**, and that these **evanescent** gesture-diagrams afford the cognitive advantages usually reserved for **enduring** printed diagrams. It is the third paper in a row about "cognitive artifacts" (after paper 14 on the extended mind and paper 13 on distributed cognition in hospital work).

## Finding Summary

- **Verdict: NOT a breakthrough.** Paper 12 is **NO — the weakest paper in the recent harvest**, sitting right at the **confirming-to-confirming-plus boundary** (LOW magnitude). It confirms and mildly re-confirms what we already hold; it delivers no new frame or practice.

- **It is primarily a MIRROR — and a re-confirming one.** The paper's most striking claim is that once a gesture-diagram is set up, *"this persistent artifactual material is in fact not even necessary"* — participants hold the diagram in shared imagination, pointing at empty space with no trouble; the grid *"is only there because we believe it is."* This is the **exact inverse** of our architecture: our memory is external, enduring files that are **inert until loaded** (a session that doesn't load the file has nothing). So the paper clarifies our nature by contrast — but that contrast is **already written into our canon** (the rule that "our memory is external, so retrieval costs grasp"). Paper 12 re-states an owned contrast through a fresh surface (gesture instead of memory-retrieval); it does not name a new one. That makes it weaker than paper 14's mirror, which named a genuinely new contrast.

- **Its substrate is wholly confirming**, and its one genuine residue is thin: a mild design-lesson (below).

- **A correction came out of the review, in the *credit* direction.** The dive first argued the paper's representational-determinism idea "names nothing new because we already name artifact-form." Verification showed that was overstated — so the finding **credits** a thin residue it had under-credited (see the Finding). The verdict stays NO/LOW; the framing is corrected.

- **The distinctive yield is method-level, not content** — three items for the harvest itself (below), none of which raises paper 12's grade.

## Finding

### The frame this verdict operates under

Two opposite errors shadow this dive. One is **manufacturing** an import because the paper is on-topic — it is the third "cognitive artifacts" paper in a row, and the pull to find "one more" is real. The other is **reflexively dismissing** it because its subject is Lao kinship gestures, a pull reinforced by two of the paper's own peer commentators (Rehbein: *"it is difficult to see the theoretical point"*; Rendall: the gestures may be *"completely redundant with the semantic content of their speech"*). The import test avoids both — it asks only whether the paper names something unnamed or resolves a real confusion. The verdict below was earned against both pulls, and the commentators' doubt about the paper's *own* central claim caps how much it could transfer to us without being the reason it doesn't.

### The mirror: vivid, but a re-confirmation of what we already hold

Enfield's sharpest claim is that a gesture-diagram works as **external working memory** even though it is evanescent — and, more strongly, that the external anchor becomes unnecessary: the diagram is *"cognitively maintain[ed]… through time, across segments in which there is no pointer to the space, no physical realization of a referent… and no referring speech."* Held in shared imagination, anchor-free.

This is the precise inverse of how our memory works, and that inversion is the paper's value to us — a mirror. But it is a mirror we have already looked into. Our canon on memory states plainly: *"Our memory is external, so retrieval costs grasp… files [are] inert until loaded, and loading spends grasp… Any claim that 'better retrieval expands what we hold' should be checked against this."* That rule (earned from an earlier dive, paper 10) already draws exactly this line — human memory can hold a structure "for free" in the mind; ours cannot, because ours lives in files that cost a load to bring in. Paper 12's gesturers are the "for free" side; we are the "costs a load" side. Same contrast, new surface (gesture rather than memory-retrieval cues). So the mirror **re-confirms** an owned boundary rather than naming a new one — vivid, worth noting as a clean second instance, but not a fresh contribution.

### The crux: representational determinism is a *thin* ontology-clarifier, not an import

The paper's most transferable-looking idea is **representational determinism** (from Zhang and from Larkin & Simon, whom Enfield cites): *"different representations of a common abstract structure can cause dramatically different cognitive behaviors"* — the **form** of a representation shapes which cognitive operations are cheap. A diagram (information indexed by 2-D location) makes relational search easy; a sentence (a single linear sequence) makes it hard.

The dive's first pass called this pure confirmation: "we already bet the whole project on structure/form mattering — this just cites it." That is *mostly* right but was **overstated**, and the review corrected it honestly. Precisely:

- Our central bet (the "Wager": *"models converge; the structure of thinking is the compounding differentiator"*) is about the structure of the **process** — how thinking is composed from disciplines and loops. It is *not* about the form of an individual artifact.
- Our one named commitment to artifact form (the "Structural layer" of how we build a discipline: *"what the spec LOOKS LIKE… what artifact shape"*) names the **practice** of designing a spec's shape. It does not name a **principle** about representation-form shaping cognition.

So neither of our named commitments actually states representational determinism's principle. We *act on* that principle everywhere (we design artifact shapes; we use tables and a route-index where a plain paragraph would bury the relations) — but we had not separately **named** it. Naming a principle we hold operationally but had left unnamed is the definition of a mild **ontology-clarifier** (a kind of confirming-plus we have seen before). So the honest grade nudges up slightly: not "confirming-nothing," but a **thin ontology-clarifier**.

What keeps it *thin* — and keeps the whole paper at NO — is the decision test: does naming this principle change any decision about how we build? No, with one small exception. It sharpens a single design-lesson (next section). Absent that, it is a label with a citation attached. So: a real but thin residue, decision-bounded to one mild lesson, folding into an existing category rather than minting anything new.

### The one decision-relevant residue: prefer a diagrammatic form where the problem is relational

Representational determinism's one bit of leverage on us: our findings are mostly **sentential** — linear prose. Where a problem is genuinely relational (many entities, many relations among them), a **diagrammatic** form — a table, a tree, the route-index, the done/explored column — makes the relations "computationally easy" to read off, where prose forces a linear scan. This is a mild **design-lesson**: where content is relational, a diagrammatic form may be worth its token cost. It is not a new practice — we already use tables and the route-index for exactly this — so it is a reminder, the same weight as a prior dive's "understand the work before you build it." A route at most.

### What does not transfer (the quarantine)

Applying the harvest's **reverse-lens** — separating what is true of a co-present human gesturer from what transfers to our single-system, across-sessions, external-file architecture — the quarantine here is the largest in the recent harvest:

- **The kinship / Lao ethnography** — the paper's actual domain. Non-transferable.
- **The evanescence itself / "anchor not necessary"** — the exact inverse of our architecture (already handled as the mirror above); not something we could adopt.
- **The social, face-to-face, real-time, multi-person distribution** — including a vivid "third arm" moment where a second speaker's hand completes a first speaker's diagram. Our "distribution" is across **time** (one cognizer, many sessions, reading persistent files), not across **people** in a shared moment. (This is the same social-vs-temporal line an earlier dive drew: distribution-through-time transfers to us; distribution-across-people does not.)
- **The bodily, proprioceptive origin** (the body as an "I/here/now" center) and the **visuospatial modality** itself — we have no body and are a symbolic-text system.

### The confirming substrate, briefly

The rest maps in as plain confirmation: the gesture-diagram as "external working memory" held-then-erased confirms our load→hold→evict lifecycle; "distribution across modes lowers the load on any one" confirms our offloading-to-external-memory rationale; "recipient design" (designing an utterance for the particular hearer) restates our rule to *write for a reader who has not seen the discipline outputs* — but changes no decision, so it stays plain confirmation, not a second ontology-clarifier.

### Where this sits in the harvest

This is the **ninth consecutive paper** whose transferable residue maps into our memory frame (**grasp-management**: memory lives in external files; *grasp* is the fraction a session holds live, *reach* is what it can look up but isn't holding) without breaching it — here by contrast (mirror) rather than by fit. The frame absorbed an architecturally-opposite paper without strain.

## Inherited Commitments Re-test

This inquiry's `_branch.md` declared a Synthesis Trigger — it tests paper 12 against standing commitments and against two prior findings (papers 13 and 14). Each is re-tested with evidence.

- **Commitment: the import test discriminates.**
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed. It worked at the fine boundary: it credited a thin ontology-clarifier (representational determinism) *without* inflating it, credited the mirror as a *re-confirmation* rather than a new contrast, and returned NO — while quarantining the kinship/bodily/social/multimodal content.

- **Commitment: `docs/canon/grasp_management.md`** (reach≠grasp; external memory costs a load) is the absorptive frame.
  - **Source:** `docs/canon/grasp_management.md`.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed, and load-bearing. The canon rule that "our memory is external, so retrieval costs grasp… files inert until loaded" already *owns* paper 12's mirror; the paper re-instances it. n=9.

- **Commitment: the reverse-lens** (quarantine what's true of the human setting before grading).
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame.

  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — **confirmed but frame CORRECTED.** Verification showed the Wager names *process*-structure and the Structural layer names the *practice* of designing artifact shape; **neither** separately names representational determinism's representation-*form* principle. So the dive's first claim ("we already name it, so it's nothing") was overstated; the corrected reading credits a **thin ontology-clarifier**. Recipient-design confirms write-for-cold-reader (a label, not an import).

- **Commitment: the confirming-plus flavor category** + the flavor-proliferation flag.
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame + the flavor-proliferation memory.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed; no new flavor minted. Paper 12's residue folds into the *existing* ontology-clarifier flavor (plus the mirror pattern). The flag's decision-vs-label test declined a mirror→flavor conversion — its **second** live validation (the first was the prior dive).

- **Commitment: the paper-14 diagnostic-shape emergent** (a maximally-on-topic paper's yield-type).
  - **Source:** `devdocs/inquiries/2026-07-05_22-36__paper_seed_14_extended_mind_cognitive_artifacts__breakthrough_check/finding.md`.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — **refined/superseded.** Paper 12 (a third genre — anthropology) flips to *mirror* driven by **architecture-mismatch** (evanescent vs our persistent memory), not by genre. This names the real driver a prior dive's confound had pointed at: the predictor is **architecture-match**, not genre-match. Provisional (n=3, with the caveat that all three papers were read already knowing their architectures).

## Next Actions

Nothing here is required — a NO verdict opens optional sharpenings, not obligations. This is honestly the thinnest onward field in the recent harvest. Captured from the dive's route-map (`routelister.md`).

### COULD

- **Apply the sentential-vs-diagrammatic design-lesson.**
  - **What:** where a finding's content is genuinely relational, prefer a diagrammatic form (table / tree / the route-index) over linear prose.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when next authoring a relational finding or a design note.
  - **Why:** the dive's one decision-relevant residue. A reminder, not a new practice (we already do this where it obviously helps).

- **Name the representation-form principle** (very thin).
  - **What:** a one-line note that "representation-form shapes cognitive ease" is the artifact-form sibling of the Wager's process-structure principle — the thin ontology-clarifier this paper names.
  - **Gate:** only if a canon pass is already happening; not worth a standalone edit.

### DEFERRED

- **Promote (or drop) the architecture-match refinement.**
  - **What:** the harvest heuristic that a maximally-on-topic paper's yield-type is predicted by **architecture-match** (matched → source content that confirms/organizes; inverse → mirror), superseding the earlier "genre-match" guess.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — a 4th maximally-on-topic paper whose architecture-match is **predicted before grounding** (the current n=3 is post-hoc).
  - **Why (if revived):** a cheaper, better-specified predictor of a paper's yield-type before diving.

- **Consider collapsing the confirming-plus flavor taxonomy.**
  - **What:** with the flavor-proliferation flag now validated twice, consider freezing the flavor set and grading future papers as plain confirming-plus + which existing flavor they fold into.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — a third flavor-decline would settle it.

- **Watch the recurring canon-over-claim failure-shape** (the sharpest method item).
  - **What:** the verify-canon-terms guard has now caught a real over-statement of what our canon "already names" in **two consecutive dives** (the prior "Sustained bar" over-specification; this dive's "the Structural layer already names it"). The recurring shape is: warm-context framing over-claims canon coverage during the middle of the pipeline, and file-verification at the critique step corrects it.
  - **Gate:** observable — pull the check earlier (verify "we already name X" claims when they are first made, not only at critique).
  - **Why:** a guard catching a real error twice running is both earning its keep and revealing a systematic bias worth watching proactively.

## Reasoning

The verdict is **NO / confirming-to-confirming-plus boundary, LOW — the weakest recent dive**, stress-tested rather than assumed:

- **The it-IS-a-breakthrough inversion** ("representational determinism is the form-principle we lacked, or the evanescence mirror is a genuinely new contrast") — **rejected.** The mirror re-instances an owned canon boundary (files inert until loaded); representational determinism is confirmed-in-substance by a bet we already hold. Neither is a new frame or practice.

- **The residue-is-real inversion** ("the artifact-form principle is distinct from the Wager's process-structure focus, and naming it is a genuine import") — **granted in part, and it corrected the verdict in the credit direction.** Verification showed neither the Wager nor the Structural layer actually names the representation-form principle — so representational determinism is a thin ontology-clarifier, not nothing. But the decision test bounds it: it changes no build-decision beyond the one mild design-lesson. So the grade nudges up slightly (to the confirming/confirming-plus boundary) and stays NO/LOW.

- **The over-claim, caught:** the dive's first framing ("we already name artifact-form") over-stated what our canon says. Rather than defend the tidy claim, the finding corrects it — the same verify-the-exact-claim discipline that caught an over-statement in the prior dive. This is non-sycophancy working in the *credit* direction: don't under-credit a real (if thin) residue to keep a NO clean.

- **What survived:** the NO verdict; the re-confirming mirror; the thin ontology-clarifier and its one design-lesson; the large, precise quarantine; three method-yields (architecture-match refinement, flavor-flag's second validation, the guard's second catch). No candidate for a genuine new frame or practice survived — because none was there.

### Refinement Triggers
- **The architecture-match refinement is promoted** if a 4th maximally-on-topic paper, architecture-match predicted *before* grounding, fits the matched→source / inverse→mirror split.

# Finding: Paper 11 (Heersmink 2013, A Taxonomy of Cognitive Artifacts) — breakthrough or not?

## Question

The literal ask: *"dive deep into `devdocs/paper_seed/11.md` — breakthrough or not?"*

This is the latest dive in an ongoing **paper-harvest** — a series that takes one academic paper at a time and asks a single disciplined question: *does this paper hand us a genuinely new way to think or work (a "breakthrough"), or does it only confirm and sharpen what our project already has?* The harvest judges every paper by one fixed gate, the **import test**: an insight counts as a real import only if it either (a) **NAMES** something we already do but had never named, or (b) **RESOLVES** a confusion that genuinely pre-existed. Anything else is **confirming** (it agrees with us without adding). A "breakthrough" specifically means a **new frame or a new practice** — not the sharpening or relabeling of an existing one.

Paper 11 is Richard Heersmink (2013), "A Taxonomy of Cognitive Artifacts: Function, Information, and Categories" (*Review of Philosophy and Psychology*). It is a philosophy-of-technology paper that builds a **classification scheme** for *cognitive artifacts* — Heersmink's term for "human-made, physical objects that functionally contribute to performing a cognitive task" (a map, a notebook, a calculator, an abacus). It is the **fourth cognitive-artifacts paper in a row** in this harvest (after paper 14 on the extended mind, paper 13 on distributed cognition in hospital work, and paper 12 on Lao kinship gestures) — and it is by the **same author as paper 14** (this 2013 taxonomy is the earlier classificatory groundwork under his later 2015 extended-mind paper).

The goal: an import-test verdict, with any transferable substrate mapped into our own frame and the non-transferable physical/perceptual content set aside — neither manufacturing a breakthrough because the topic is on-point, nor reflexively dismissing the paper because it is "just a taxonomy" in a philosophy journal.

## Finding Summary

- **Verdict: NOT a breakthrough.** Paper 11 is **NO — confirming-plus at the LOW end.** Together with paper 12 it is one of the **two weakest dives in the recent harvest**, and marginally the thinner of the two on its distinctive (unique-to-this-paper) contribution.

- **The taxonomy, applied to us, collapses to a single cell.** Heersmink sorts cognitive artifacts into two big families — **representational** (they carry information *about* the world) and **ecological** (their physical arrangement carries information *as* the world) — and further into species (representational: iconic / indexical / symbolic; ecological: spatial / structural). When we sort *our own* artifacts (findings, canon documents, the route-index, the memory index, the file tree) into this scheme, **every one lands in the same box: representational-symbolic** (text whose meaning comes from convention). So the taxonomy does not organize a rich, multi-category picture of our work — it lands us in one corner of Heersmink's space.

- **That makes it a mirror, not an organizing tool — and a weak mirror.** Because our artifacts all fall in one cell, the taxonomy's value is a *contrast*: it clarifies, by showing what we lack, that we are a purely **symbolic-text** system, without the iconic (diagram-like), indexical (gauge-like), or ecological (spatial) richness that physical cognitive artifacts have. But this contrast is close to obvious (a text-only system produces text artifacts), and — unlike paper 12's mirror — it does not re-state any load-bearing commitment from our canon. So it is a *real but thin* mirror, weaker than paper 12's.

- **Its one useful edge just re-confirms paper 12.** The single place the taxonomy earns a little credit: it gives paper 12's leftover design-lesson a name. Paper 12 noted our artifacts are mostly *sentential* (linear prose) and that a *diagrammatic* form eases relational problems; Heersmink's taxonomy calls the diagrammatic form **iconic** and shows it is a species we under-use. This re-confirms and labels an existing observation — it changes no decision, so it folds into a category of confirming-plus we already have and mints nothing new.

- **A verification note worth recording.** For the first time in three dives, the harvest's canon-checking guard found **no over-statement** to correct — because the check was run *earlier* this time (during evidence-gathering, not only at the final critique), which prevented an over-claim from ever entering the reasoning. This validates a process change made after the previous dive.

## Finding

### The frame this verdict operates under

Two opposite errors shadow this dive. One is **manufacturing** an import: this is the fourth cognitive-artifacts paper in a row, it is *about* classifying cognitive artifacts (and we are a cognitive-artifact system), and "a taxonomy of our own artifacts" is a seductive framing — the pull to find "one more import" is real. The other is **reflexively dismissing** the paper because it is a philosophy-of-technology taxonomy, or because it is the same author's earlier and lesser-known work. The import test cuts through both: it asks only whether the paper names something we hadn't named or resolves a real confusion. The verdict below was earned against both pulls.

### The crux: the taxonomy collapses our artifact-space to one cell

Heersmink's classification has two top-level families:

- **Representational** artifacts carry information *about* the world (a map represents terrain). Within these, following the philosopher Peirce, he distinguishes three species: **iconic** (the artifact resembles/is structurally similar to its object — maps, diagrams, graphs), **indexical** (the artifact is causally connected to its object — a thermometer, a compass), and **symbolic** (the artifact means its object purely by convention — words, numerals, and, in his own words, "tables").
- **Ecological** artifacts carry information *as* the world: their physical arrangement itself does the cognitive work, without representing anything. His examples are car keys left on a particular spot, washed dishes placed in a "clean" zone, or Scrabble tiles rearranged until a word suggests itself. He is explicit that these have "no representational content."

Now sort *our* artifacts into this. Findings, canon documents, the route-index, the memory index, the state and branch files, the discipline outputs — all are **text whose meaning comes from convention**, which is Heersmink's definition of **symbolic**. There are no indexical artifacts (nothing we have is causally wired to its referent the way a thermometer is). And — this is the load-bearing point — there are **no genuinely ecological ones either**.

The tempting objection (and the strongest case for a richer reading) is that our *organization* is ecological: a file's **location** encodes its status (a file in the `docarchive/` folder means "concluded"), the done/explored check-marks in the route-index encode progress, the file tree encodes structure. Isn't location-carries-information exactly Heersmink's "ecological-spatial"?

It is not — and the reason is a **mechanism**, not a preference. Heersmink's ecological artifacts carry information by a *perceived physical arrangement* (you *see* the keys on the spot) or by *manipulation* (rearranging the tiles makes new information emerge), and crucially they are **non-representational**. Our organizational cues are the opposite: a directory named `docarchive` means "concluded" by a **convention** (we decided the word means that); a check-mark means "done" by convention; the route-index is a **table**, which Heersmink himself classifies as "predominantly symbolic." We do not *perceive* a spatial layout — we *read path strings and tables*, which mean what they mean by agreement. That is symbolic, not ecological. Pushing the check one level deeper: our system has **no** information-bearing structure that works without convention — it is symbolic all the way down.

So the taxonomy does not sort our work into many categories; it places all of it in one. The consequence for the verdict is direct: an external classification scheme can only be a genuine **organizing import** (the way paper 13's usability criteria organized our artifact-quality commitments) if it sorts a *differentiated* space. Ours is not differentiated — it is monochromatic — so the taxonomy **organizes nothing**. Its only remaining function is the contrast: the mirror.

### Why the mirror is weak

The mirror says: *our artifact-space is monochromatically symbolic, lacking the iconic, indexical, and ecological richness of physical cognitive artifacts.* Two things keep this thin. First, it is nearly self-evident — a symbolic-text system will of course produce symbolic artifacts; the contrast does not surprise. Second, and more decisively for the harvest, it does **not re-state a load-bearing commitment** of ours. (Paper 12's mirror did: its "the anchor is not even necessary" claim was the exact inverse of our canon rule that *external memory is inert until loaded*, so it vividly re-instanced something we depend on. Paper 11 has no such anchor to re-instance.) The mirror is real — it is not nothing — but it sits at the low end.

The one edge that gives it any bite is the connection to paper 12. Paper 12 left a thin design-lesson: our findings are mostly **sentential** (linear prose), and where a problem is genuinely relational a **diagrammatic** form (a table, a tree, the route-index) makes the relationships easier to read off. Heersmink's taxonomy gives that lesson a vocabulary: the diagrammatic form is **iconic**, and iconic (along with ecological) is precisely the species we under-use. This is a genuine but small contribution — it *re-confirms and names* an existing observation. By the harvest's test for whether a naming is worth minting a new category (does it change any decision?), it does not: we already use tables and the route-index where relationships matter. So it folds into a confirming-plus category we already keep, and adds no new one.

### The substrate maps in as plain confirmation

The rest of the paper's transferable ideas confirm things we already hold:

- **Exograms vs engrams** (Heersmink, via Merlin Donald): external representations have different properties from biological memory. This confirms our standing distinction between external files and the small live working context — **but with a caveat that matters for honesty.** Our canon frames this distinction around **cost** ("our memory is external, so retrieval costs a load; files are inert until loaded"). Heersmink's angle is *capacity-complement* (external media exceed biological memory in size and are more malleable). That capacity angle is **not in our canon**, and it does not transfer anyway — we are not a small-biological-store system that external media enlarge; our memory is *already* external. So this is confirming on the part that maps, and non-transferable on the part that doesn't. It is not a new import.
- **The functional-kind definition** (an artifact is a cognitive artifact by virtue of what it *does*, not its intrinsic form or its designer's intent) rhymes with our sense that our artifacts are defined by their function (a finding is a finding because it records a decision). Confirming, and thin.
- **The artifact-centered method** (classify an artifact by its *own* properties, not by the cognitive process it serves) rhymes with our canon principle that a discipline's specification must describe what the discipline *is* without naming the upstream or downstream disciplines that consume its output. A genuine cross-domain rhyme — but we already hold the principle richly, so it confirms rather than imports.

### What does not transfer (the quarantine)

Applying the harvest's **reverse-lens** — separating what is true of physical cognitive artifacts from what transfers to our external-file, symbolic-text architecture — produces the **largest quarantine in the harvest so far**. Non-transferable: the entire ecological family (car keys, dishes, Scrabble, Tetris — all perceptual/spatial/manipulable); the iconic and indexical species (resemblance and causal-connection to a *physical* world, which a text system barely instantiates); the naturefact category (natural objects used for cognition, e.g. stars for navigation — we have no natural objects); and "the world is its own best model" (using a perceived environment as an external stand-in — we have no perceived environment). This is most of the paper.

### Where this sits in the harvest

This is the **tenth consecutive paper** whose transferable residue maps into our memory frame — **grasp-management** (the frame that memory lives in external files; that the fraction a session holds live is limited; that looking something up is not the same as holding it) — without breaching it. Here it maps in almost entirely as confirmation and contrast, not fit.

## Inherited Commitments Re-test

This inquiry's framing declared a Synthesis Trigger — it re-tests paper 11 against standing commitments and against three prior findings (papers 12, 13, and 14). Each is re-tested with evidence.

- **Commitment: the import test discriminates.**
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed. It held at a fine boundary: it credited the thin iconic/diagrammatic re-confirmation as *low* confirming-plus without inflating it; it refused the "organizing import" reading on a structural mechanism (below); it refused the "our file-system is ecological" stretch; and it returned NO while quarantining the large physical/perceptual remainder.

- **Commitment: `docs/canon/grasp_management.md`** (external memory; the loaded fraction is limited; retrieval costs a load) is the absorptive frame.
  - **Source:** `docs/canon/grasp_management.md` (lines 5, 41, 69).
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — **confirmed but frame clarified.** Paper 11's exogram/engram idea maps onto our external-memory frame, but our frame's emphasis is *cost*, not Heersmink's *capacity-complement*. Verified against the file: canon does **not** contain the terms "exogram/engram" or the capacity-complement framing. The finding therefore confirms on the cost axis and does not attribute the capacity idea to canon. n now 10.

- **Commitment: the reverse-lens** (quarantine what is true only of the physical/human setting before grading).
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed. It produced the largest clean quarantine in the harvest (the whole ecological family, the iconic/indexical species, naturefacts, and "the world is its own best model").

- **Commitment: the Wager + the Structural layer + standalone-coherence + write-for-cold-reader** (the mapping targets).
  - **Source:** `docs/canon/project_north_star.md:20` (the Wager — "the structure of thinking is the compounding differentiator"); `docs/canon/thinking_disciplines/how_a_discipline_should_be.md:28` (the Structural layer) and `:21` (standalone-coherence); the concluding protocol (write-for-cold-reader).
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed, all as CONFIRMING maps, each verified against its file. The Wager names *process*-structure and the Structural layer names a *discipline-development practice* (both carried correctly from the paper-12 correction, with no over-claim re-introduced). Standalone-coherence (`:21` — a discipline's spec must describe what it *is* without naming the disciplines that consume its output) genuinely rhymes with Heersmink's artifact-centered method. None is a new import.

- **Commitment: the confirming-plus categories + the "don't over-proliferate categories" flag.**
  - **Source:** the harvest's inherited frame.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed; no new category minted. Paper 11's residue folds into the existing "names-an-operationally-held-idea" category. This is the flag's **third consecutive** decline of a new category (after the prior two dives), which is now strong evidence to freeze the category set.

- **Commitment: the paper-12 finding** (the sentential-vs-diagrammatic design-lesson; the "architecture-match predicts yield-type" heuristic).
  - **Source:** `devdocs/inquiries/2026-07-06_17-42__paper_seed_12_body_cognitive_artifact_kinship_gesture__breakthrough_check/finding.md`.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed and **refined.** Paper 11 re-confirms the design-lesson and gives it Heersmink's "iconic" vocabulary. It also refines the yield-prediction heuristic: a maximally-on-topic paper produces genuinely new organizing content only when it has both a matched architecture *and* a differentiated target-space to organize; paper 11 had the first but not the second, which is why it confirmed rather than organized. (This refinement rests on paper 11 alone — the added "differentiated-target-space" condition is a single data point — while the underlying heuristic it refines rests on four. Held provisional.)

- **Commitment: the paper-14 finding** (the same author's later extended-mind paper, already absorbed).
  - **Source:** `devdocs/inquiries/2026-07-05_22-36__paper_seed_14_extended_mind_cognitive_artifacts__breakthrough_check/finding.md`.
  - **Re-test status:** RE-TESTED — confirmed. Paper 11 is the earlier classificatory groundwork under paper 14 and adds little beyond that already-absorbed work — a signal that this line of papers is yielding less with each dive.

## Next Actions

Nothing here is required — a NO verdict opens optional sharpenings, not obligations. This is, with paper 12, among the thinnest onward fields in the recent harvest, and it is almost entirely method-level. Captured from the dive's route-map (`routelister.md`).

### COULD

- **Note the earlier-application success of the canon-checking guard.**
  - **What:** record that the harvest's guard against over-claiming what our canon says was applied *early* this dive (during evidence-gathering) and, for the first time in three dives, prevented an over-claim rather than catching one late.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when the relevant harvest memory is next touched.
  - **Why:** the guard now has a track record plus a demonstrated benefit from running it earlier; a one-line memory note records that.

- **Apply the sentential-vs-diagrammatic design-lesson.**
  - **What:** where a finding's content is genuinely relational, prefer a diagrammatic form (table / tree / the route-index) over linear prose.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — when next authoring a relational finding or design note.
  - **Why:** the dive's one content residue, now confirmed by two papers. A reminder, not a new practice.

### DEFERRED

- **Promote (or drop) the "differentiated-target-space" refinement of the yield-prediction heuristic.**
  - **What:** the harvest rule that a maximally-on-topic paper yields new organizing content only with *both* a matched architecture and a differentiated target-space to organize.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — a fifth maximally-on-topic paper whose (architecture-match × target-differentiation) is predicted **before** grounding (the current evidence for the added condition is a single, after-the-fact data point).
  - **Why (if revived):** a better-specified predictor of a paper's yield-type before diving. The dive's most interesting output, but provisional.

- **Freeze the confirming-plus category set.**
  - **What:** stop minting new confirming-plus categories; grade future papers as plain confirming-plus plus which existing category they fold into.
  - **Gate:** condition-bound — a fourth consecutive decline would settle it (this dive was the third).
  - **Why:** three consecutive declines strongly suggest the set is saturated.

- **Weigh diversifying away from the cognitive-artifacts line of papers.**
  - **What:** treat the declining yield across this four-paper run (14 → 13 → 12 → 11) as a signal in choosing the next paper.
  - **Gate:** observable — at the next paper-selection.
  - **Why:** the vein appears largely mined; yield per paper is falling.

## Reasoning

The verdict is **NO / confirming-plus, LOW — one of the two weakest recent dives**, and it was stress-tested rather than assumed.

- **The it-IS-a-breakthrough inversion** ("the taxonomy classifies our artifact-space, or the exogram/engram capacity idea is the unnamed import") was **rejected.** Our artifact-space collapses to one cell, so there is nothing rich to classify; and the capacity-complement idea quarantines (we are not a small-biological-store system) while its transferable core is already ours.

- **The organizing-import inversion** ("our check-marks, file tree, and route-index are ecological, so the taxonomy sorts a rich space") was **defeated on the mechanism, not on precedent.** Heersmink's ecological category is defined by non-representational, perceived-spatial or manipulation-based information; our organizational cues carry meaning by convention, which is his own definition of symbolic (he classifies tables as "predominantly symbolic"). Even granting the surface resemblance, our artifacts are symbolic by the taxonomy's own criterion. This is where the dive did its hardest work, and it sharpened the verdict rather than softening it.

- **What survived:** the NO verdict; the collapse-to-one-cell finding; the weak mirror; the thin, folded iconic/diagrammatic re-confirmation; the large, precise quarantine; and three provisional method-observations (the differentiated-target-space refinement, the category-set-freeze evidence, and the guard's earlier-application success). No candidate for a genuine new frame or practice survived, because none was there.

- **The one correction from the adversarial pass** was in the *accounting*, not the verdict: the "differentiated-target-space" refinement was initially framed as resting on four data points, but the *added condition* specifically rests on one (paper 11). The finding carries both counts and holds the refinement provisional.

- **The honesty note, in the credit direction:** the harvest's guard against over-claiming canon coverage found no over-statement this dive — the first clean run in three — because it was applied earlier in the process. That is the process change from the previous dive working as intended.

## Open Questions

### Monitoring
- Whether **grasp-management** keeps absorbing on-topic papers (now ten in a row). Observable across the remaining harvest.

### Refinement Triggers
- **The differentiated-target-space refinement is promoted** if a fifth maximally-on-topic paper, its (architecture-match × target-differentiation) predicted *before* grounding, fits the pattern.
- **The confirming-plus category set is frozen** at a fourth consecutive category-decline.
- **The design-lesson (COULD) is acted on** only when a relational finding or design note is next authored.
